as_polyhedra(data, fields=None)

A shape-based dataset as a polyhedral one, every cell a polyhedron.

Its derived faces already hold every face once, in side 0's outward order (a voxel's pixel faces as quads), with the side of each cell's reference, so they become the polyhedral faces as they stand: face ids, and so fields on faces, are unchanged. Edges come out numbered as before. Cells must be 3D, and neighbours wound alike: an inside-out cell beside an upright one is refused, since their shared face would have them on one side. Constant and H1 order-1 fields, values on points, cells, faces and edges, and sets carry over; fields needing a reference element are dropped.

@on_inputs_device
def as_polyhedra(data, fields=None):
    """A shape-based dataset as a polyhedral one, every cell a polyhedron.

    Its derived faces already hold every face once, in side 0's outward order
    (a voxel's pixel faces as quads), with the side of each cell's reference, so
    they become the polyhedral faces as they stand: face ids, and so fields on
    faces, are unchanged. Edges come out numbered as before. Cells must be 3D,
    and neighbours wound alike: an inside-out cell beside an upright one is
    refused, since their shared face would have them on one side.
    ``Constant`` and ``H1`` order-1 fields, values on points, cells, faces and
    edges, and sets carry over; fields needing a reference element are dropped.
    """
    from tack.dataset.spaces import H1

    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1) or data.geometry.space.order != 1:
        raise TypeError("as_polyhedra needs an order-1 H1 geometry: positions per point")
    topology = data.topology
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"{group.shape.__name__} cells are not 3D: a polyhedral "
                             "topology is of 3D cells (as_polygons takes 2D ones)")
    faces = topology.faces()
    same_way = tack.zeros((1,), tack.i32)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _same_way(data.domain_view("cells", group), same_way)
    if same_way[0]:
        raise ValueError(f"{same_way[0]} faces are wound the same way by both their cells "
                         "(an inside-out cell beside an upright one, as cell_geometry's "
                         "negative measures show); a polyhedral topology needs each face's "
                         "cells on opposite sides of it")
    nf = faces.num_faces
    idt = topology.id_dtype
    # The faces' points: 4 a face, past 12 a cell when faces are not shared (a
    # hexahedron has 24), and the polyhedral topology holds twice that.
    fdt = ids.at_least(idt, 8 * nf)
    sizes = tack.empty((nf,), tack.i32)
    starts = tack.empty((nf + 1,), fdt)
    if nf:
        _face_sizes(faces.kinds, sizes)
    total = exclusive_scan(sizes, starts, nf, close=True)
    face_points = tack.empty((total,), fdt)
    if nf:
        _face_rows(faces.rows, starts, sizes, face_points)

    n = data.num_cells
    counts = tack.zeros((n,), tack.i32)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _cell_face_counts(group.view(), counts)
    cell_offsets = tack.empty((n + 1,), idt)
    entries = exclusive_scan(counts, cell_offsets, n, close=True)
    cell_faces = tack.empty((entries,), idt)
    cell_face_sides = tack.empty((entries,), tack.u8)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _cell_face_entries(data.domain_view("cells", group), cell_offsets, cell_faces,
                               cell_face_sides)
    out = PolyhedralTopology(starts, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces, cell_face_sides,
                             num_points=data.num_points)

    # The same points, cells and faces (in the shape path's numbering), so the
    # sets still apply; edges too, both paths numbering them by (low, high)
    # point ids.
    return carry(data, out, points=Same(), cells=Same(), faces=Same(), edges=Same(),
                 fields=fields)

@on_inputs_device
def as_polygons(data, fields=None):
    """A shape-based dataset of 2D cells -- triangles, quads, pixels -- as a polygonal
    one: each cell's points in order become its loop. Fields carry as
    ``as_polyhedra``'s do, but values on faces and edges, whose numbering the
    polygonal topology derives afresh, are dropped. A polygonal dataset comes
    back as it is (a new dataset on the same topology)."""

    topology = data.topology
    if isinstance(topology, PolygonalTopology):
        return carry(data, topology, points=Same(), cells=Same(), fields=fields)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"{group.shape.__name__} cells are not 2D")
    n = data.num_cells
    idt = topology.id_dtype
    sizes = tack.zeros((n,), tack.i32)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _polygon_sizes(group.view(), sizes)
    offsets = tack.empty((n + 1,), idt)
    total = exclusive_scan(sizes, offsets, n, close=True)
    loops = tack.empty((total,), idt)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _polygon_loops(group.view(), offsets, loops)
    out = PolygonalTopology(offsets, loops, num_points=data.num_points)
    # The same points and cells; edge numbering is derived afresh.
    return carry(data, out, points=Same(), cells=Same(), fields=fields)

@on_inputs_device
def shrink(data, factor=0.5, fields=None):
    """Every cell shrunk toward its centroid (the mean of its corners) by ``factor``,
    as Viskores' Shrink and VTK's vtkShrinkFilter. Viskores gives each cell its
    own copies of its points; here that is an ``L2`` geometry on the same
    topology, and point data becomes ``L2`` the same way (each cell's own copy
    of its corners' values). Everything else is kept, the topology's faces and
    edges with it."""

    if not 0 <= factor <= 1:
        raise ValueError(f"factor must lie in [0, 1], not {factor!r}")
    corners = project(data, data.geometry, L2(data))
    if data.num_cells:
        _shrink_corners(corners.values, corners.space.offsets, float(factor), data.num_cells)
    from tack.dataset.carry import selected

    out = {}
    for name in selected(data, fields):
        f = data.fields[name]
        space = f.space
        if isinstance(space, Values) and space.on == "points":
            f, space = Field(H1(data), f.values, f.unit), H1(data)
        out[name] = project(data, f, L2(data)) if isinstance(space, H1) else f
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(data, DataSet(data.topology, corners, fields=out, sets=dict(data.sets)))

    ``vtkCellGridToUnstructuredGrid`` gives one (for export, rendering, or a filter

    geometry and fields. A lattice point shared by cells is one point, its value
    computed once (on an ``L2`` geometry each cell's points are its own). ``H1`` and ``L2`` fields become point data (an ``L2`` field's
    value at a shared point from one of its cells); cell fields go to every
    sub-cell of their cell. Segments, quads, pixels, hexahedra and voxels."""
    names = list(data.fields) if fields is None else list(fields)
    level = default_level(data, *(data.fields[name] for name in names)) if level is None \
        else int(level)
    if level < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"subdivide's level is at least 1, not {level}")
    flags = tack.empty((data.num_cells,), tack.i32)
    if data.num_cells:
        for_each(_all_cells, data, "cells", flags)
    refined, _ = _refined(data, flags, level, {name: data.fields[name] for name in names})
    return refined

docs.text:
transform(data, matrix, fields=None)

The geometry under an affine map: a 4x4 matrix (its last row 0 0 0 1) or 3x4, applied to each position as a column (Viskores' PointTransform, VTK's vtkTransformFilter). On a dataset with an origin the map moves the origin, in double precision, and only its linear part acts on the geometry's values, so a rotation far from zero loses nothing.

An image stays an image: the map is folded into its origin and direction (UniformCoordinates; the direction may be any invertible matrix, a shear too), in double precision, and no position is stored -- as VTK's image data with a direction matrix holds it. A singular map (a projection) gives the positions themselves.

@on_inputs_device
def transform(data, matrix, fields=None):
    """The geometry under an affine map: a 4x4 matrix (its last row 0 0 0 1) or 3x4,
    applied to each position as a column (Viskores' PointTransform, VTK's
    vtkTransformFilter). On a dataset with an origin the map moves the origin,
    in double precision, and only its linear part acts on the geometry's values,
    so a rotation far from zero loses nothing.

    An image stays an image: the map is folded into its origin and direction
    (``UniformCoordinates``; the direction may be any invertible matrix, a shear
    too), in double precision, and no position is stored -- as VTK's image data
    with a direction matrix holds it. A singular map (a projection) gives the
    positions themselves."""
    m = np.asarray(matrix, float)
    if m.shape == (4, 4):
        if not np.allclose(m[3], [0, 0, 0, 1]):
            raise ValueError("a projective matrix (last row not 0 0 0 1) is not affine")
        m = m[:3]
    if m.shape != (3, 4):
        raise ValueError(f"transform takes a 4x4 or 3x4 matrix, not {m.shape}")
    origin = None
    if any(data.origin):
        origin = m[:, :3] @ np.asarray(data.origin) + m[:, 3]
        m = np.hstack([m[:, :3], np.zeros((3, 1))])
    values = data.geometry.values
    # A singular map (a projection) flattens the image: its positions are stored.
    if isinstance(values, UniformCoordinates) and np.linalg.det(m[:, :3]) != 0.0:
        image = UniformCoordinates(values.dims, m[:, :3] @ np.asarray(values._origin) + m[:, 3],
                                   values._spacing, m[:, :3] @ values._matrix,
                                   dtype=data.dtype, device=data.device)
        out = _moved(data, image, fields)
        if origin is not None:
            out.origin = origin
        return out
    n = size_of(values)
    out = _vectors(n, data.dtype)
    if n:
        _affine(data.geometry.values, *map(float, m.reshape(-1)), out)
    out = _moved(data, out, fields)
    if origin is not None:
        out.origin = origin
    return out

direction may also be an H1 field of higher order than the geometry (a finite-element displacement, as MFEM's examples displace their meshes): the geometry is first carried into its space (project, exact for the lower order), so the output's geometry is curved, in that space; scale_by is then in that space too.

@on_inputs_device
def warp(data, direction, scale=1.0, scale_by=None, fields=None):
    """The geometry moved along ``direction`` -- a 3-vector field in the geometry's
    space (or its name), or one 3-vector for every point -- times ``scale``
    and, if given, a scalar field ``scale_by`` in the same space (Viskores'
    Warp; VTK's vtkWarpVector and vtkWarpScalar). Values on points are that
    space when the geometry is order-1 ``H1`` (``surface_normals``' normals). A
    2-vector field (a 2D problem's displacement) moves x and y.

    ``direction`` may also be an ``H1`` field of higher order than the geometry
    (a finite-element displacement, as MFEM's examples displace their meshes):
    the geometry is first carried into its space (``project``, exact for the
    lower order), so the output's geometry is curved, in that space; ``scale_by``
    is then in that space too."""
    geometry = data.geometry
    dtype = data.dtype
    if isinstance(direction, (str, Field)):
        direction = data.fields[direction] if isinstance(direction, str) else direction
        direction = _with_basis(data, direction)
        if width_of(direction.values) not in (2, 3):
            raise ValueError("direction must be a 3-vector field in the geometry's space "
                             "(or a 2-vector one, moving x and y)")
        if direction.space is not geometry.space:
            geometry = _lifted(data, geometry, direction.space)
    n = size_of(geometry.values)
    factors = (scale_by if not isinstance(scale_by, str) else data.fields[scale_by])
    if factors is None:
        factors = ConstantArray(1.0, n, dtype=dtype, device=data.device)
    else:
        factors = _with_basis(data, factors)
        if factors.space is not geometry.space or width_of(factors.values):
            raise ValueError("scale_by must be a scalar field in the geometry's space")
        factors = factors.values
    out = _vectors(n, dtype)
    if isinstance(direction, Field):
        if n:
            moving = _warp_by_field if width_of(direction.values) == 3 else _warp_in_plane
            moving(geometry.values, direction.values, factors,
                   float(scale), out)
    else:
        d = np.asarray(direction, float).reshape(-1)
        if d.size != 3:
            raise ValueError("a constant direction is three numbers")
        if n:
            _warp_constant(geometry.values, *map(float, d), factors,
                           float(scale), out)
    return _moved(data, out, fields, space=geometry.space)

docs.title: cell_geometry
docs.text:
cell_geometry(data)

CellGeometry(measure, centroid) of each cell: fields on cells. A 3D cell's volume, by the divergence theorem over its faces -- polyhedral or of a shape -- with faces taken as fans from their points' means, so a cell with non-planar faces is measured as that polyhedron (a hexahedron with warped faces is not quite its trilinear volume); its faces must be wound out of it. A 2D cell's area -- triangle, quad, pixel or polygon -- along its own normal (Newell's), from its edges going round it. A line's or a polyline's length, and the centroid of its segments; a vertex's point, with measure 0.

On a curved geometry (H1 above order 1, or an L2 one of order 2 or more) each cell is measured as it is, by quadrature through its own map (integrate.cell_measures): its volume, area or length, and the centroid those weigh. (A curved cell was measured by its corners.)

@on_inputs_device
def cell_geometry(data):
    """``CellGeometry(measure, centroid)`` of each cell: fields on cells. A 3D cell's volume, by the
    divergence theorem over its faces -- polyhedral or of a shape -- with faces
    taken as fans from their points' means, so a cell with non-planar faces is
    measured as that polyhedron (a hexahedron with warped faces is not quite its
    trilinear volume); its faces must be wound out of it. A 2D cell's area --
    triangle, quad, pixel or polygon -- along its own normal (Newell's), from
    its edges going round it. A line's or a polyline's length, and the
    centroid of its segments; a vertex's point, with measure 0.

    On a curved geometry (``H1`` above order 1, or an ``L2`` one of order 2 or
    more) each cell is measured as it is, by quadrature through its own map
    (``integrate.cell_measures``): its volume, area or length, and the centroid
    those weigh. (A curved cell was measured by its corners.)"""
    space = data.geometry.space
    if getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True) and (
            (isinstance(space, H1) and space.order > 1)
            or (isinstance(space, L2) and space.tensor)):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.integrate import cell_measures

        volumes, centroids = cell_measures(data)
        return CellGeometry(Field(Values(data, "cells"), volumes, _measure_unit(data)),
                            Field(Values(data, "cells"), centroids, data.unit))
    if data.topology.dimension > 1 and not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        data.topology.faces()                      # polyhedra and polygons walk theirs
    n = data.num_cells
    volumes = tack.empty((n,), data.dtype)
    centroids = _vectors(n, data.dtype)
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == 3:
            _cell_geometry(data.domain_view("cells", group), volumes, centroids)
        elif group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION < data.topology.dimension and \
                group.shape in _ROUND:
            _corner_polygon_geometry(data.domain_view("cells", group),
                                     _table(("round", group.shape), _ROUND[group.shape]),
                                     volumes, centroids)
        elif group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == 2:
            _polygon_geometry(data.domain_view("cells", group), volumes, centroids)
        elif group.count and group.shape is shapes.PolyLine:
            _line_geometry(data.domain_view("cells", group), volumes, centroids)
        elif group.count:
            _corner_geometry(data.domain_view("cells", group), volumes, centroids)
    return CellGeometry(Field(Values(data, "cells"), volumes, _measure_unit(data)),
                        Field(Values(data, "cells"), centroids, data.unit))

A 3D mesh's faces are polygons of any size, the normal the mean one on a non-planar face; a 2D mesh's faces are edges, the normal in the plane of side 0's cell and the "area" the edge's length; a polyline mesh's faces are the polylines' ends, the normal along the line out of side 0 and the "area" 1.

@on_inputs_device
def face_geometry(data):
    """``FaceGeometry(normal, area)``: fields on faces. A face's normal points out of
    its side 0. A 3D mesh's faces are polygons of any size, the normal the mean
    one on a non-planar face; a 2D mesh's faces are edges, the normal in the
    plane of side 0's cell and the "area" the edge's length; a polyline mesh's
    faces are the polylines' ends, the normal along the line out of side 0 and
    the "area" 1."""
    faces = data.topology.faces()
    dtype = data.dtype
    normals = _vectors(faces.num_faces, dtype)
    areas = tack.empty((faces.num_faces,), dtype)
    dimension = data.topology.dimension
    if dimension in (1, 2):
        # Faces of a 2D or 1D mesh are its cells' sides; cells of a lower
        # dimension (a surface's lines, a line mesh's vertices) have none.
        kernel = _edge_geometry if dimension == 2 else _end_geometry
        for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
            if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == dimension:
                kernel(data.domain_view("cells", group), normals, areas)
    else:
        for_each(_face_geometry, data, "faces", normals, areas)
    # A face of a k-dimensional mesh measures k - 1 dimensions; a polyline end's
    # "area" is 1.
    area = units.derived((data.unit, data.topology.dimension - 1))
    return FaceGeometry(Field(Values(data, "faces"), normals, "dimensionless"),
                        Field(Values(data, "faces"), areas, area))

def cell_centers(data):

    That is ``values_at_centers(data, data.geometry)``, and not the centroid on a
    cell that is not affine; ``cell_geometry(data).centroid`` is the centroid, on

docs.title: cell_quality
docs.text:
cell_quality(data, measures=None)

How well shaped each cell is: a dict of cell fields, one per measure named in measures (all of MEASURES by default). Each is 1 on the ideal cell of its shape (equilateral; a cube, a regular tetrahedron, an equilateral wedge and pyramid), as Verdict (VTK's vtkMeshQuality) defines it where it does:

  • scaled_jacobian: the least, over the cell's corners (and a hexahedron's center), of the determinant of its edges there, each scaled to unit length, relative to the ideal cell's: 1 ideal, 0 degenerate (an edge of no length at a corner, or a flat cell; Verdict gives its largest value for such a hexahedron), negative inverted.
  • jacobian_ratio: the least corner determinant over the greatest; 1 for a cell whose Jacobian is constant (every simplex), 0 where every corner is degenerate, negative where one corner is inverted.
  • condition: the greatest, over the corners, condition number of the corner's edges against the ideal cell's (|T| |T^-1| / d, T = A W^-1, Frobenius norms): 1 ideal, growing as the cell distorts, infinite (the largest float) where a corner is degenerate or inverted.
  • edge_ratio: the longest edge over the shortest.
  • min_edge, max_edge: the shortest and longest edge, in the spatial unit.

The corners' edges are the geometry's Jacobian there applied to the reference cell's edge directions, so an order-2 (curved) cell is measured along its curved edges at its corners. A pyramid, which has no Jacobian at its apex, is measured as Verdict does, by its four tetrahedra over both base diagonals. Polyhedra and polygons, which have no reference cell, are measured by the fan tetrahedra and triangles Tack evaluates them in, each against the regular tetrahedron or equilateral triangle, except that a polygon of three or four points is measured as the triangle or quad it is. Their Jacobian measures (scaled Jacobian, Jacobian ratio, condition) are therefore on the fan's scale, not the shapes': a cube as a polyhedron has a scaled Jacobian of 0.58 and a condition of 1.29 where the hexahedron has 1 and 1, and no polyhedron has an ideal to score 1 against. Read them as a validity check -- a positive scaled Jacobian when every fan tetrahedron is upright (the cell star-shaped from its points' mean), zero or negative when one is flat or inverted -- and compare polyhedra with each other, not with shaped cells. The edge measures mean the same on every cell. Lines and vertices have no Jacobian measures (NaN); a line's edges are its segments. Hidden cells are measured like the rest.

Matched to VTK 9.7.1's vtkMeshQuality to rounding for the scaled Jacobian of every linear shape, the condition number of triangles, quads, tetrahedra and hexahedra, and the edge ratio of triangles, quads, tetrahedra and wedges. VTK's wedge condition number and hexahedron edge ratio differ (see the tests).

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/cell_quality.py

    measured as Verdict does, by its four tetrahedra over both base diagonals.
    Polyhedra and polygons, which have no reference cell, are measured by the fan
    tetrahedra and triangles Tack evaluates them in, each against the regular
    tetrahedron or equilateral triangle, except that a polygon of three or four
    points is measured as the triangle or quad it is. Their Jacobian measures
    (scaled Jacobian, Jacobian ratio, condition) are therefore on the fan's
    scale, not the shapes': a cube as a polyhedron has a scaled Jacobian of 0.58
    and a condition of 1.29 where the hexahedron has 1 and 1, and no polyhedron
    has an ideal to score 1 against. Read them as a validity check -- a positive
    scaled Jacobian when every fan tetrahedron is upright (the cell star-shaped
    from its points' mean), zero or negative when one is flat or inverted -- and
    compare polyhedra with each other, not with shaped cells. The edge measures
    mean the same on every cell. Lines and vertices have no Jacobian measures
    (NaN); a line's edges are its segments. Hidden cells are measured like the

    and hexahedra, and the edge ratio of triangles, quads, tetrahedra and wedges.
    VTK's wedge condition number and hexahedron edge ratio differ (see the
    tests)."""

                _pyramid_quality(view, norms, inverses, big, sj, ratio, cond)
            edges = _table("pyramid edges", _PYRAMID_EDGES)
            _edges_by_table(view, edges, lo, hi)
        elif shape is shapes.Polyhedron:
            if jacobian:
                w = tack.array(np.linalg.inv(_REGULAR).astype(dtype.numpy_dtype).reshape(-1))
                _polyhedron_quality(view, w, big, sj, ratio, cond)
            _edges_by_sides(view, lo, hi)
        elif shape is shapes.Polygon:
            if jacobian:
                _polygon_quality(view, big, sj, ratio, cond)
            _edges_by_sides(view, lo, hi)
        else:
            # Lines, polylines, vertices: no Jacobian measures.
            _no_jacobian(view, float("nan"), sj, ratio, cond)
            if shape is shapes.PolyLine:
                _edges_of_lines(view, lo, hi)
            else:
                _edges_by_table(view, _table(("line edges", shape is shapes.Line),
                                             [0, 1] if shape is shapes.Line else [0, 0]), lo, hi)
    if "edge_ratio" in names:
        out["edge_ratio"] = tack.empty((n,), dtype)
        if n:
            _ratio(out["min_edge"], out["max_edge"], big, float("nan"), out["edge_ratio"])
    space = Values(data, "cells")
    units = {"min_edge": data.unit, "max_edge": data.unit}
    return {m: Field(space, out[m], units.get(m, "dimensionless")) for m in names}

Each geometry value's position along the line from low_point to high_point, clamped to it and mapped to range (VTK's vtkElevationFilter, Viskores' PointElevation): a field in the geometry's space. The two points are world positions, taken relative to the dataset's origin in double precision.

@on_inputs_device
def point_elevation(data, low_point=(0, 0, 0), high_point=(0, 0, 1), range=(0.0, 1.0)):
    """Each geometry value's position along the line from ``low_point`` to
    ``high_point``, clamped to it and mapped to ``range`` (VTK's
    vtkElevationFilter, Viskores' PointElevation): a field in the geometry's
    space. The two points are world positions, taken relative to the dataset's
    origin in double precision."""
    low = np.asarray(low_point, float) - np.asarray(data.origin)
    direction = np.asarray(high_point, float) - np.asarray(data.origin) - low
    length2 = float(direction @ direction)
    if length2 == 0:
        raise ValueError("the low and high points must differ")
    n = size_of(data.geometry.values)
    out = _scalars(n, data.dtype)
    if n:
        # The geometry as it is: an image's or a grid's positions are computed as
        # they are read, never stored.
        _elevations(data.geometry.values, *map(float, low), *map(float, direction),
                    length2, float(range[0]), float(range[1] - range[0]), out)
    return Field(data.geometry.space, out)

@on_inputs_device
def implicit_values(data, function):
    """``function``, an implicit function (``tack.dataset.implicit``: ``Plane``,
    ``Sphere``, ``Box``, ...), at the geometry's values: a field in the
    geometry's space and type, negative inside the function's region. On an
    ``H1`` geometry that is one value per point. The function is in world
    positions, taken relative to the dataset's origin in double precision."""
    positions = data.geometry.values             # an image's computed as they are read
    n = size_of(data.geometry.values)
    dtype = arrays.dtype_of(data.geometry.values)
    out = tack.empty((n,), dtype)
    # A function holding arrays (Planes) gives a copy at the data's precision and
    # on its device; the others hold Python numbers, which take it anyway.
    from tack.dataset.implicit import relative_to

    function = relative_to(function, data.origin)    # the geometry's values are relative
    matching = getattr(type(function), "_matching", None)
    if matching is not None:
        function = matching(function, dtype, data.device)
    if n:
        _implicit_values(positions, function, out)
    return Field(data.geometry.space, out)

docs.title: gradients
docs.text:
gradients(data, field, at='cells')

The gradient of field -- H1, L2 or Constant, scalar or vector -- at each cell's parametric center (at="cells") or at the points (at="points": each cell's gradient at the point, averaged over the cells around it, as VTK's vtkGradientFilter and Viskores' point gradients do).

A scalar gives a 3-vector per entity; a vector of k components 3k values, row by row -- d(u_i)/d(x_j) at 3 * i + j, the layout of VTK's and Viskores' gradient tensors.

at may instead be an L2 space of the dataset: the gradient at each of its nodes in each cell -- a discontinuous field, exact at the nodes, so an H1 field of order p keeps its order's detail in L2 of order p, where a gradient at the points averages it away. The field's basis gives its derivative in parametric coordinates and the geometry's Jacobian turns that into a world gradient, so the two need not share a space. A 2D cell's gradient lies in its plane (VTK's and Viskores' in-plane gradient), lines and vertices get zero, and a cell of no volume or area NaN (its Jacobian is singular). flow_quantities derives divergence, vorticity and the Q-criterion from a vector field's gradient.

On a polyhedral topology there is no reference element. A cell's gradient of point data is then Green-Gauss over its boundary: the faces walked outward and fanned from their points' means (the triangles cell_geometry measures the volume by), each triangle's area vector times the mean of its values, over the volume. That is exact for a linear field and needs no interpolant. Cell data, constant in each cell, has a zero gradient there, as on shapes. A polygon's is the same in its plane, over its edges; polylines get zero. At the points, the cells' gradients are averaged over the cells around each point.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/gradients.py 
@on_inputs_device
def gradients(data, field, at="cells"):
    """The gradient of ``field`` -- ``H1``, ``L2`` or ``Constant``, scalar or vector --
    at each cell's parametric center (``at="cells"``) or at the points
    (``at="points"``: each cell's gradient at the point, averaged over the cells
    around it, as VTK's vtkGradientFilter and Viskores' point gradients do).

    A scalar gives a 3-vector per entity; a vector of ``k`` components ``3k``
    values, row by row -- ``d(u_i)/d(x_j)`` at ``3 * i + j``, the layout of
    VTK's and Viskores' gradient tensors.

    ``at`` may instead be an ``L2`` space of the dataset: the gradient at each of
    its nodes in each cell -- a discontinuous field, exact at the nodes, so an
    ``H1`` field of order ``p`` keeps its order's detail in ``L2`` of order ``p``,
    where a gradient at the points averages it away. The field's basis gives its
    derivative in parametric coordinates and the geometry's Jacobian turns that
    into a world gradient, so the two need not share a space. A 2D cell's
    gradient lies in its plane (VTK's and Viskores' in-plane gradient), lines
    and vertices get zero, and a cell of no volume or area NaN (its Jacobian is
    singular). ``flow_quantities`` derives divergence, vorticity and
    the Q-criterion from a vector field's gradient.

    On a polyhedral topology there is no reference element. A cell's gradient
    of point data is then Green-Gauss over its boundary: the faces walked
    outward and fanned from their points' means (the triangles ``cell_geometry``
    measures the volume by), each triangle's area vector times the mean of its
    values, over the volume. That is exact for a linear field and needs no
    interpolant. Cell data, constant in each cell, has a zero gradient there,
    as on shapes. A polygon's is the same in its plane, over its edges; polylines
    get zero. At the points, the cells' gradients are averaged over the cells
    around each point."""
    field = _with_basis(data, _field(data, field))
    if (not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True)
            and not isinstance(field.space, (H1, Constant))):
        raise NotImplementedError(f"gradients of a field on {field.space!r} on a mesh "
                                  "without reference elements: point or cell data only")
    if isinstance(at, L2):
        if at.topology is not data.topology:
            raise ValueError("gradients at the nodes of a space of another topology")
        if not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
            raise NotImplementedError("gradients at an L2 space's nodes take cells with a "
                                      "reference element")
        space = at
    elif at not in ("cells", "points"):
        raise ValueError(f"gradients are at 'cells' or 'points', or an L2 space's nodes, "
                         f"not {at!r}")
    else:
        space = Values(data, at)
    # Per unit length; a difference of degrees Celsius is in kelvin.
    unit = units.derived(units.delta(field.unit), (data.unit, -1))
    width = width_of(field.values)
    if not width:
        return Field(space, _scalar_gradients(data, field, at), unit)
    n = space.size if isinstance(at, L2) else data.num_cells if at == "cells" \
        else data.num_points
    out = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(3 * width, data.dtype))
    values = materialize(field.values)
    for k in range(width):
        part = tack.empty((size_of(field.values),), arrays.dtype_of(field.values))
        if part.shape[0]:
            _component(values, k, part)
        rows = _scalar_gradients(data, Field(field.space, part), at)
        if n:
            _place_rows(rows, k, out)
    return Field(space, out, unit)

@on_inputs_device
def flow_quantities(data, gradient):
    """Divergence, vorticity and the Q-criterion from the gradient of a 3-vector field
    (``gradients`` of it: 9 values per entity), in the gradient's space, as VTK's
    vtkGradientFilter and Viskores' Gradient compute them, as ``FlowQuantities``:
    ``divergence``, ``vorticity`` and ``q_criterion``."""
    gradient = _field(data, gradient)
    if width_of(gradient.values) != 9:
        raise TypeError("flow_quantities takes the gradient of a 3-vector field (9 values)")
    n = size_of(gradient.values)
    dtype = arrays.dtype_of(gradient.values)
    divergence = tack.empty((n,), dtype)
    vorticity = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(3, dtype))
    q = tack.empty((n,), dtype)
    if n:
        _flow_quantities(materialize(gradient.values), divergence, vorticity, q)
    unit = gradient.unit
    return FlowQuantities(Field(gradient.space, divergence, unit),
                          Field(gradient.space, vorticity, unit),
                          Field(gradient.space, q, units.derived((unit, 2))))

docs.title: project
docs.text:
project(data, field, space)

field (a Field or a name) in space, a space of the same topology: a new field. Values on points or cells count as order-1 H1 and Constant, both as source and as target.

Into H1, each node takes the mean of the source evaluated there by the cells around it: the source's own value wherever it is continuous (so a continuous field of lower order comes across exactly), and an average where cells disagree -- a cell field's, as vtkCellDataToPointData takes it, or a DG field's corner values. Into Constant (or order-0 L2), each cell takes the mean of its corner values, as vtkPointDataToCellData does. Into order-1 L2, each cell takes the source's values at its corners, exactly whatever the source's order is up to 1. Into SideTraces, each face side the source's values from its cell (traces). Sums run in a fixed order, so results do not vary from run to run.

Values on faces or edges have no basis to project, and are refused as a source or target. On polyhedra, polygons and polylines -- no reference element -- only cell values and point values project, one into the other, each cell averaging over its distinct points. The values must be floating point, scalars or vectors, except from order-1 H1 into order-1 L2, which copies them and takes integers too.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/project.py 
@on_inputs_device
def project(data, field, space):
    """``field`` (a ``Field`` or a name) in ``space``, a space of the same topology:
    a new field. Values on points or cells count as order-1 ``H1`` and
    ``Constant``, both as source and as target.

    Into ``H1``, each node takes the mean of the source evaluated there by the
    cells around it: the source's own value wherever it is continuous (so a
    continuous field of lower order comes across exactly), and an average where
    cells disagree -- a cell field's, as vtkCellDataToPointData takes it, or a DG
    field's corner values. Into ``Constant`` (or order-0 ``L2``), each cell takes
    the mean of its corner values, as vtkPointDataToCellData does. Into order-1
    ``L2``, each cell takes the source's values at its corners, exactly whatever
    the source's order is up to 1. Into ``SideTraces``, each face side the
    source's values from its cell (``traces``). Sums run in a fixed order, so
    results do not vary from run to run.

    Values on faces or edges have no basis to project, and are refused as a
    source or target. On polyhedra, polygons and polylines -- no reference
    element -- only cell values and point values project, one into the other,
    each cell averaging over its distinct points. The values must be floating
    point, scalars or vectors, except from order-1 ``H1`` into order-1 ``L2``,
    which copies them and takes integers too.
    """
    field = _with_basis(data, _field(data, field))
    source = field.space
    if space.topology is not data.topology:
        raise ValueError("project moves a field between spaces of one topology")
    if isinstance(space, Values) and space.on in ("points", "cells"):
        projected = project(data, field, H1(data) if space.on == "points" else Constant(data))
        return Field(space, projected.values, field.unit)
    for which, s in (("from", source), ("into", space)):
        if not s.interpolated:
            raise TypeError(f"project works {which} a space with a basis, or values on the "
                            f"points or cells; {s!r} has no basis to project")
    if isinstance(source, SideTraces):
        raise TypeError("a field of traces has two values on each face; project the field "
                        "they were taken from")
    values = field.values
    if space is source:
        return Field(space, _take(values, tack.arange(space.size, dtype=data.id_dtype)),
                     field.unit)
    if dtype_of(values) not in (tack.f32, tack.f64):
        if (isinstance(space, L2) and not space.varies and space.order == 1
                and isinstance(source, H1) and source.order == 1
                and getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True)):
            out = _like(values, space.size)
            for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [field]):
                if group.count:
                    _corner_copies(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group),
                                   space.offsets, out)
            return Field(space, out, field.unit)
        raise TypeError(f"project averages and interpolates floating-point values, not "
                        f"{dtype_of(values).name}")
    if isinstance(space, SideTraces):
        return traces(data, field)
    from tack.dataset import _bernstein

    if _bernstein.is_bernstein(space):
        # Into the equispaced nodes, then their Bernstein coefficients.
        nodal = project(data, field, _bernstein.lagrange_companion(space))
        return _bernstein.from_lagrange(data, nodal, space)
    if not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        if isinstance(space, H1) and space.order == 1 and isinstance(source, Constant):
            return Field(space, _onto_points(data, field, values), field.unit)
        if isinstance(space, Constant) and isinstance(source, H1) and source.order == 1:
            out = _like(values, data.num_cells)
            for_each(_distinct_point_means, data, "cells", materialize(values), out)
            return Field(space, out, field.unit)
        reference_cells(data.topology, f"project from {source!r} to {space!r}")
    if isinstance(space, H1):
        if space.order == 1:
            return Field(space, _onto_points(data, field, values), field.unit)
        return Field(space, _onto_nodes(data, field, space, values), field.unit)
    out = _like(values, space.size)
    if isinstance(space, Constant) or (isinstance(space, L2) and not space.varies
                                       and space.order == 0):
        for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [field]):
            if group.count:
                _cell_means(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group), out)
        return Field(space, out, field.unit)
    target = Field(space, out)
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [field, target]):
        if group.count:
            kernel = _cell_nodes
            if getattr(space, "tensor", False):
                kernel = (_tensor_cell_nodes if bases.tensor_shape(group.shape)
                          else _lattice_cell_nodes)
            kernel(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group), target.view(group),
                   space.offsets, out)
    return Field(space, out, field.unit)

@on_inputs_device
def values_at_centers(data, field):
    """``field`` evaluated at each cell's parametric center, through its basis.

    On a polyhedron, polygon or polyline, which have no reference element, the
    center is the cell point (see ``cell_centers``) and point data (``H1``)
    takes its value there, the mean of the cell's distinct points' values: the
    value of the cell's interpolant, linear on tetrahedra fanned from that
    point. Cell data (``Constant``) is its own value."""
    field = _with_basis(data, _field(data, field))
    out = _like(field.values, data.num_cells)
    if getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        for_each(_at_centers, data, "cells", field, out)
    elif isinstance(field.space, H1) and field.space.order == 1:
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.project import _distinct_point_means

        for_each(_distinct_point_means, data, "cells", materialize(field.values), out)
    elif isinstance(field.space, Constant):
        tack.copyto(out, materialize(field.values))
    else:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"values_at_centers of {field.space!r} on polyhedra, "
                                  "polygons or polylines: only point data (H1, order 1) and "
                                  "cell data (Constant) have values there")
    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, field.unit)

docs.text:
interpolate(data, function, space, dtype=None, unit=None)

A Field in space whose values are function at each of the space's nodes: function is a @tack.func of a world position (a 3-vector of the geometry's type) returning a scalar or a vector, and dtype its result's type -- data.dtype by default, tack.vec3() for 3-vectors.

The nodes are where the geometry puts them, evaluated as needed and never stored: H1's points (and at order 2 its edge middles, quad face centers and cell centers), L2's cell corners (order 1) or parametric centers (order 0), Constant's and Values(data, "cells")' parametric centers, Values(data, "points")' points. A node shared by several cells is evaluated once, by the first cell that has it, so a discontinuous (L2) geometry gives a shared node the first cell's position. A point no cell uses takes function at its own position when the geometry is H1, otherwise zero.

A function of position is what the space can represent exactly when it is a polynomial of the space's order on straight cells; otherwise this is the space's nodal interpolant. On polyhedra, polygons and polylines -- no reference element -- only point values (H1 of order 1 and Values(data, "points")) of an H1 geometry interpolate.

unit is the values' unit (Field.unit): a function's code does not say it, so by default it is unknown.

@on_inputs_device
def interpolate(data, function, space, dtype=None, unit=None):
    """A ``Field`` in ``space`` whose values are ``function`` at each of the space's
    nodes: ``function`` is a ``@tack.func`` of a world position (a 3-vector of
    the geometry's type) returning a scalar or a vector, and ``dtype`` its
    result's type -- ``data.dtype`` by default, ``tack.vec3()`` for 3-vectors.

    The nodes are where the geometry puts them, evaluated as needed and never
    stored: ``H1``'s points (and at order 2 its edge middles, quad face centers
    and cell centers), ``L2``'s cell corners (order 1) or parametric centers
    (order 0), ``Constant``'s and ``Values(data, "cells")``' parametric
    centers, ``Values(data, "points")``' points. A node shared by several
    cells is evaluated once, by the first cell that has it, so a discontinuous
    (``L2``) geometry gives a shared node the first cell's position. A point no
    cell uses takes ``function`` at its own position when the geometry is
    ``H1``, otherwise zero.

    A function of position is what the space can represent exactly when it is
    a polynomial of the space's order on straight cells; otherwise this is the
    space's nodal interpolant. On polyhedra, polygons and polylines -- no
    reference element -- only point values (``H1`` of order 1 and
    ``Values(data, "points")``) of an ``H1`` geometry interpolate.

    ``unit`` is the values' unit (``Field.unit``): a function's code does not say
    it, so by default it is unknown."""
    if not isinstance(function, Func):
        raise TypeError(f"interpolate takes a @tack.func of position, not {function!r}")
    if space.topology is not data.topology:
        raise ValueError("interpolate takes a space of the dataset's own topology")
    if isinstance(space, Values) and space.on not in ("points", "cells"):
        raise TypeError(f"interpolate gives values at points or cells, not on {space.on}")
    if not isinstance(space, (H1, L2, Constant, Values)):
        raise TypeError(f"interpolate takes H1, L2, Constant or Values, not {space!r}")
    from tack.dataset import _bernstein

    # A curved Bernstein geometry's values are control points: nodes are placed on
    # its values at the equispaced nodes instead.
    data = _bernstein.with_lagrange_geometry(data)
    if _bernstein.is_bernstein(space):
        # Values at the equispaced nodes, then their Bernstein coefficients.
        nodal = interpolate(data, function, _bernstein.lagrange_companion(space), dtype, unit)
        return _bernstein.from_lagrange(data, nodal, space)
    fn = _Of(function, data.origin)
    values = tack.zeros((space.size,), dtype or data.dtype)
    out = Field(space, values, unit)
    if isinstance(space, H1) and space.dofs is not None:
        _into_table(data, fn, space, out)
        return out
    shared = isinstance(space, H1) or (isinstance(space, Values) and space.on == "points")
    if not (shared and not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1)):
        # Every node once, from the space's node views.
        for_each(_at_space_nodes, data, space, fn, values)
        return out
    # An L2 geometry gives a shared node no position of its own: the first cell
    # that has it decides, through its corners.
    reference_cells(data.topology, f"interpolate into {space!r}")
    if isinstance(space, Values):
        raise ValueError("an L2 geometry has positions per cell corner, not per point")
    starts, writers = _writers(data, space, out)
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [out]):
        if not group.count:
            continue
        cells = data.domain_view("cells", group)
        if space.order == 1:
            _at_corners(cells, fn, writers, starts[group.root], values)
        else:
            _at_nodes(cells, out.view(group), fn, writers, starts[group.root], 0, values)
    return out

@on_inputs_device
def composite(data, *fields):
    """Scalar fields of one space as the components of one vector field (Viskores'
    CompositeVectors), in the order given. The fields must be in one unit, the
    vector's (an unknown one is not checked)."""
    fields = [_field(data, f) for f in fields]
    if len(fields) < 2:
        raise ValueError("composite takes at least two scalar fields")
    space, n = _same_space(*fields)
    if any(width_of(f.values) for f in fields):
        raise TypeError("composite takes scalar fields")

convert(data, unit, field=None)

data -- a Field, or a dataset -- in unit. A field gives a new field in the same space, its values scaled (and offset, as from degrees Celsius to kelvin) on the device. A dataset gives a new dataset with field (a name) in unit, or its geometry when field is None, the topology, sets, marks and other fields kept.

The field's unit, or the spatial unit, must be known (Field.unit, DataSet.unit) and of unit's dimensions. Converting the geometry scales the origin too, in double precision on the host, so survey coordinates in US survey feet become metres without losing digits; an image stays an image and a rectilinear grid keeps its axes. Positions are the dataset's to convert: the geometry field alone would leave the origin in the old unit. Integer fields are refused unless the conversion is a relabelling ("1000*m" to "km").

@on_inputs_device
def convert(data, unit, field=None):
    """``data`` -- a ``Field``, or a dataset -- in ``unit``. A field gives a new
    field in the same space, its values scaled (and offset, as from degrees
    Celsius to kelvin) on the device. A dataset gives a new dataset with
    ``field`` (a name) in ``unit``, or its geometry when ``field`` is ``None``,
    the topology, sets, marks and other fields kept.

    The field's unit, or the spatial unit, must be known (``Field.unit``,
    ``DataSet.unit``) and of ``unit``'s dimensions. Converting the geometry
    scales the origin too, in double precision on the host, so survey
    coordinates in US survey feet become metres without losing digits; an
    image stays an image and a rectilinear grid keeps its axes. Positions are
    the dataset's to convert: the geometry field alone would leave the origin
    in the old unit. Integer fields are refused unless the conversion is a
    relabelling (``"1000*m"`` to ``"km"``)."""
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._moving import _moved

    target = units.canonical(unit)
    if isinstance(data, Field):
        if field is not None:
            raise TypeError("convert of a field takes no field name: give the dataset and "
                            "the name, or the field alone")
        return _converted(data, target, "the field")
    if field is None:
        factor, offset = units.conversion(data.unit, target)
        if offset:
            raise ValueError(f"positions in {data.unit!r} are not lengths with a zero")
        values = data.geometry.values
        if isinstance(values, UniformCoordinates):
            moved = UniformCoordinates(values.dims, np.asarray(values._origin) * factor,
                                       np.asarray(values._spacing) * factor,
                                       values._matrix if values.ORIENTED else None,
                                       dtype=values.dtype, device=data.device)
        elif isinstance(values, CartesianProduct):
            axes = [arrays.to_host(axis).astype(np.float64).reshape(-1) * factor
                    for axis in (values.xs, values.ys, values.zs)]
            moved = CartesianProduct(*axes, dtype=values.dtype, device=data.device)
        else:
            moved = _times(values, factor, 0.0)
        out = _moved(data, moved)
        out._geometry = Field(out.geometry.space, out.geometry.values, target)
        out.origin = np.asarray(data.origin) * factor
        return out
    if not isinstance(field, str):
        raise TypeError(f"convert takes a field's name, not {field!r}")
    if field not in data.fields:
        raise KeyError(f"no field {field!r}: the dataset has "
                       f"{', '.join(map(repr, data.fields)) or 'none'}")
    fields = dict(data.fields)
    fields[field] = _converted(data.fields[field], target, f"field {field!r}")
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(data, DataSet(data.topology, data.geometry, fields=fields,
                                    sets=dict(data.sets)))

docs.text:
jump(data, field)

A field's difference across each face at the face's center, side 1 minus side 0 (zero on the boundary): a field on faces. Each side is the field as its own cell's basis has it at the face's center (the mean of the face's corners in the cell's reference element, the same point from both sides), so a DG field's jumps are its own, of any order, not its cells' averages; a continuous field's are zero. Up to order 1 the face's corner values (traces) give the center exactly; above it, the corners' linear mean was wrong, and each side's basis is evaluated there. Cell data (Constant, values on cells) is read from each side's cell directly, on any topology, polyhedral included.

@on_inputs_device
def jump(data, field):
    """A field's difference across each face at the face's center, side 1 minus side
    0 (zero on the boundary): a field on faces. Each side is the field as its own
    cell's basis has it at the face's center (the mean of the face's corners in
    the cell's reference element, the same point from both sides), so a DG
    field's jumps are its own, of any order, not its cells' averages; a
    continuous field's are zero. Up to order 1 the face's corner values
    (``traces``) give the center exactly; above it, the corners' linear mean was
    wrong, and each side's basis is evaluated there. Cell data (``Constant``, values on
    cells) is read from each side's cell directly, on any topology, polyhedral
    included."""
    field = _field(data, field)
    faces = data.topology.faces()
    out = _like(field.values, faces.num_faces)
    if _on_cells(data, field):
        for_each(_cell_jump, data, "faces", materialize(field.values), out)
    elif getattr(field.space, "order", 1) <= 1 or getattr(field.space, "varies", False):
        # Up to order 1 a side is linear over the face, so its corner values
        # (traces) give the center exactly -- on a pyramid's triangles too, whose
        # map from the reference is not affine.
        for_each(_trace_jump, data, "faces", traces(data, field), out)
    else:
        reference_cells(data.topology, "jump")
        sides = _like(field.values, 2 * faces.num_faces)
        if faces.num_faces:
            sides.fill(0)
        for group in data.launch_groups("cells", [field]):
            if group.count:
                _side_centers(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group), sides)
        for_each(_jump, data, "faces", sides, out)
    return Field(Values(data, "faces"), out, units.delta(field.unit))

upwind_flux(data, field, velocity)

The flux of field carried by a constant velocity through each face, out of side 0: (v . n) * area * u, u taken from the upwind side at the face's center -- the side the flow leaves -- as a DG advection scheme does. A boundary face takes its one side's value whichever way the flow goes. divergence of the result is each cell's net outflow.

@on_inputs_device
def upwind_flux(data, field, velocity):
    """The flux of ``field`` carried by a constant ``velocity`` through each face, out
    of side 0: ``(v . n) * area * u``, ``u`` taken from the upwind side at the face's
    center -- the side the flow leaves -- as a DG advection scheme does. A boundary
    face takes its one side's value whichever way the flow goes. ``divergence`` of
    the result is each cell's net outflow."""
    field = _field(data, field)
    normals, areas = face_geometry(data)
    out = _like(field.values, data.topology.faces().num_faces)
    velocity, speed = units.number_and_unit(velocity)
    vx, vy, vz = (float(v) for v in velocity)
    if _on_cells(data, field):
        for_each(_cell_upwind, data, "faces", materialize(field.values), normals.values,
                 areas.values, vx, vy, vz, out)
    else:
        for_each(_upwind, data, "faces", traces(data, field), normals.values, areas.values,
                 vx, vy, vz, out)
    # (v . n) area u: a velocity given as a bare number leaves it unknown.
    area = units.derived((data.unit, data.topology.dimension - 1))
    return Field(Values(data, "faces", oriented=True), out,
                 units.named(units.derived(field.unit, speed, area)))

net_flux(data, flux)

Each cell's outward sum of flux, values on faces measured out of side 0 (Values(data, "faces", oriented=True), or plain face values taken so): a face's value counts plus for its side-0 cell and minus for its side-1 cell.

Given each face's integrated flux (upwind_flux, or a normal component times the area), it is the net outflow of each cell, V times the divergence; divergence divides by the cells' measure. Nothing is weighted: the values are summed as they are, so face area vectors sum to zero on a closed cell. Cells of a lower dimension than the mesh's have no faces: zero.

@on_inputs_device
def net_flux(data, flux):
    """Each cell's outward sum of ``flux``, values on faces measured out of side 0
    (``Values(data, "faces", oriented=True)``, or plain face values taken so): a
    face's value counts plus for its side-0 cell and minus for its side-1 cell.

    Given each face's integrated flux (``upwind_flux``, or a normal component times
    the area), it is the net outflow of each cell, ``V`` times the divergence;
    ``divergence`` divides by the cells' measure. Nothing is weighted: the
    values are summed as they are, so face area vectors sum to zero on a closed
    cell. Cells of a lower dimension than the mesh's have no faces: zero."""
    flux = _field(data, flux)
    if not _on_faces(data, flux):
        raise TypeError("net_flux sums a field on faces")
    data.topology.faces()                          # the incidence the cell views need
    out = _like(flux.values, data.num_cells)
    out.fill(0)
    # Cells of a lower dimension (a surface's triangles among tetrahedra) have
    # no faces of the mesh's, so no flux: zero. Nor has a mesh of vertices any.
    values = materialize(flux.values)
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == data.topology.dimension > 0:
            _outward_sums(data.domain_view("cells", group), values, out)
    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, flux.unit)

@on_inputs_device
def divergence(data, flux):
    """Each cell's finite-volume divergence of ``flux``, the integrated flux through
    each face out of its side 0 (``upwind_flux``, or a normal component times the
    area): ``net_flux`` over the cell's measure (``cell_geometry``), so for a
    linear field it is the field's divergence. A cell of no measure gives no
    finite value, as ``perot`` and ``gradients`` give. ``flow_quantities`` gives
    the finite-element divergence instead, the trace of a field's gradient."""
    net = net_flux(data, flux)
    measure = cell_geometry(data).measure
    out = _like(net.values, data.num_cells)
    if data.num_cells:

    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, units.derived(net.unit, (measure.unit, -1)))

@on_inputs_device
def perot(data, flux):
    """A vector per cell from each face's normal component -- Perot's reconstruction,
    ``u_c = (1/V) sum_f A_f u_f (r_f - r_c)``, as C-grid models (MPAS, ICON) need to
    show their face-normal velocity at cells.

    ``flux`` is a scalar field on faces, the component along each face's normal out
    of its side 0; the side each cell is on gives the sign. Face centers, areas
    and cell centroids and volumes are this module's, so a uniform field's normal
    components give it back exactly on cells with planar faces. First order, as
    Perot's method is. A cell of no volume gives NaN, and one of a lower dimension
    than the mesh's (no faces of it) zero."""
    flux = _field(data, flux)
    if not _on_faces(data, flux):
        raise TypeError("perot reconstructs from a field on faces")
    _, areas = face_geometry(data)
    centers = face_centers(data)
    volumes, centroids = cell_geometry(data)
    out = _vectors(data.num_cells, data.dtype)
    out.fill(0)                       # cells of a lower dimension, and vertices: no faces
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION == data.topology.dimension > 0:
            _perot(data.domain_view("cells", group), materialize(flux.values), areas.values,
                   centers.values, centroids.values, volumes.values, out)
    # Areas times offsets over volumes cancel: the components' unit.
    return Field(Values(data, "cells"), out, flux.unit)

docs.text:
statistics(data, field, weights=None, level=None)

Descriptive statistics of a scalar field's values, as Viskores' Statistics filter gives them: a Statistics of n, min, max, sum, mean, the central moment sums m2, m3, m4, sample_variance (m2 / (n - 1)), population_variance (m2 / n), their standard deviations, skewness (sqrt(n) m3 / m2^1.5) and kurtosis (n m4 / m2^2, not the excess), the last two 0 for a constant field. Moments are taken about the mean, in a second pass. Ghosts are left out: cells and points data.ghosts marks a duplicate (another piece owns them) or hidden.

Over a PartitionedDataSet, field names a field every piece has: each piece's moments, over what it owns, are taken on its own device and combined pairwise, in the order of the pieces over every rank of data.world -- the same result however the pieces are shared out. Where every shared cell and point has one owner, the result is the whole's up to rounding. Over an AMRDataSet, the same over every box of every level: refined cells and points are left out, so each region of space counts once, at its finest level. Over an OctreeDataSet, its leaves (or the nodes of one level), every rank's.

weights weighs each value: "volume", each cell's measure (a cell field's), or a scalar field on the same entities, by name (a density, for mass-weighted moments). Then mean is sum(w x) / W, sum is sum(w x), the moments are sum(w (x - mean)^k), weight is W, the sum of the weights, the population variance m2 / W, the sample variance m2 / (W - sum(w^2) / W) (reliability weights, NumPy's aweights), and skewness and kurtosis take W for n. Cells of different sizes -- an AMR hierarchy's levels, an octree's leaves -- then count by their size.

@on_inputs_device
def statistics(data, field, weights=None, level=None):
    """Descriptive statistics of a scalar field's values, as Viskores' Statistics
    filter gives them: a ``Statistics`` of ``n``, ``min``, ``max``, ``sum``, ``mean``, the
    central moment sums ``m2``, ``m3``, ``m4``, ``sample_variance``
    (``m2 / (n - 1)``), ``population_variance`` (``m2 / n``), their standard
    deviations, ``skewness`` (``sqrt(n) m3 / m2^1.5``) and ``kurtosis``
    (``n m4 / m2^2``, not the excess), the last two 0 for a constant field.
    Moments are taken about the mean, in a second pass. Ghosts are left out:
    cells and points ``data.ghosts`` marks a duplicate (another piece owns
    them) or hidden.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, ``field`` names a field every piece has: each
    piece's moments, over what it owns, are taken on its own device and
    combined pairwise, in the order of the pieces over every rank of
    ``data.world`` -- the same result however the pieces are shared out. Where
    every shared cell and point has one owner, the result is the whole's up to
    rounding. Over an ``AMRDataSet``, the same over every box of every level:
    refined cells and points are left out, so each region of space counts
    once, at its finest level. Over an ``OctreeDataSet``, its leaves (or the
    nodes of one ``level``), every rank's.

    ``weights`` weighs each value: ``"volume"``, each cell's measure (a cell
    field's), or a scalar field on the same entities, by name (a density, for
    mass-weighted moments). Then ``mean`` is ``sum(w x) / W``, ``sum`` is ``sum(w
    x)``, the moments are ``sum(w (x - mean)^k)``, ``weight`` is ``W``, the sum of
    the weights, the population variance ``m2 / W``, the sample variance
    ``m2 / (W - sum(w^2) / W)`` (reliability weights, NumPy's ``aweights``), and
    skewness and kurtosis take ``W`` for ``n``. Cells of different sizes -- an
    AMR hierarchy's levels, an octree's leaves -- then count by their size."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet
    from tack.dataset.octree import OctreeDataSet

    if isinstance(data, OctreeDataSet):
        return data._statistics(field, weights, level)
    if level is not None:
        raise TypeError("level= picks an octree's level; this is not an OctreeDataSet")
    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        data = data._as_pieces()
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        fields_of(data, field, "statistics")
        from tack.dataset import units

        # Every rank's pieces' units, so a rank holding none agrees with the rest.
        every = [pair for part in data.world._allgather(
            [_units(piece, field, weights) for piece in data]) for pair in part]
        unit = units.common("statistics' pieces' field", [u for u, _ in every])
        weight_unit = units.common("statistics' pieces' weights", [w for _, w in every])
        moments = None
        for part in _over_pieces(data, lambda piece: _moments(piece, field, weights)):
            if part is not None:
                moments = part if moments is None else _merged(moments, part)
    else:
        unit, weight_unit = _units(data, field, weights)
        moments = _moments(data, field, weights)
    if moments is None:
        raise ValueError("statistics of no values")
    return _summary(*moments)._replace(unit=unit, weight_unit=weight_unit)

docs.text:
integrate(data, fields=None)

The measure of data -- its cells' total volume, area or length -- and the integral over it of each of fields (names; by default every field with a basis or on the cells), as VTK's vtkIntegrateAttributes gives them: Integrals(measure, measure_unit, values, units), values[name] a float or a tuple for a vector field.

Each cell is integrated by Gauss quadrature in its reference element through its own map (quadrature: collapsed onto simplices and wedges), with enough points for the field's order and the geometry's, so a curved geometry and a field of any order (H1, L2, point and cell data) integrate exactly, to rounding. Polyhedra, polygons and polylines take their measure from cell_geometry and integrate cell data and point data, which is linear on their pieces (sub-tetrahedra, triangles, segments), exactly. Only the cells of the mesh's dimension count, as in VTK: a volume's integrals leave out its surfaces, lines and vertices. Only owned cells count (ghost marks), and a PartitionedDataSet sums its pieces over every rank, in the pieces' order.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/integrate.py 
@on_inputs_device
def integrate(data, fields=None):
    """The measure of ``data`` -- its cells' total volume, area or length -- and the
    integral over it of each of ``fields`` (names; by default every field with a
    basis or on the cells), as VTK's ``vtkIntegrateAttributes`` gives them:
    ``Integrals(measure, measure_unit, values, units)``, ``values[name]`` a float or
    a tuple for a vector field.

    Each cell is integrated by Gauss quadrature in its reference element through
    its own map (``quadrature``: collapsed onto simplices and wedges), with enough
    points for the field's order and the geometry's, so a curved geometry and a
    field of any order (``H1``, ``L2``, point and cell data) integrate exactly, to
    rounding. Polyhedra, polygons and polylines take their measure from
    ``cell_geometry`` and integrate cell data and point data, which is linear on
    their pieces (sub-tetrahedra, triangles, segments), exactly. Only the cells of the mesh's dimension count, as in VTK: a volume's
    integrals leave out its surfaces, lines and vertices. Only owned cells count
    (ghost marks), and a ``PartitionedDataSet`` sums its pieces over every rank, in
    the pieces' order."""
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._common import _measure_unit
    from tack.dataset.partitioned import PartitionedDataSet

    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.statistics import _over_pieces

        pieces = list(data)
        names = _names(pieces[0], fields) if pieces else []
        parts = _over_pieces(data, lambda piece: _piece(piece, names))
        measure = math.fsum(m for m, _ in parts)
        values = {name: np.sum([v[name] for _, v in parts], axis=0) for name in names}
        first = pieces[0] if pieces else None
    else:
        names = _names(data, fields)
        measure, values = _piece(data, names)
        first = data
    out_units = {name: units.derived((first.fields[name].unit, 1),
                                     (_measure_unit(first), 1)) if first is not None else None
                 for name in names}
    return Integrals(measure=measure, measure_unit=_measure_unit(first) if first else None,
                     values={name: (float(v) if np.ndim(v) == 0 else tuple(map(float, v)))
                             for name, v in values.items()},
                     units=out_units)

unit_of(name)

The unit of the statistic name ("mean", "sum", ...), or None if unknown: min, max and mean are in the values' unit, sum in it times the weights', the moment sums m2 ... m4 in its powers times the weights', the variances in its square and the standard deviations in it (a difference of degrees Celsius is in kelvin), skewness, kurtosis and n pure numbers, weight in the weights' unit.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/statistics.py 
def unit_of(self, name):
    """The unit of the statistic ``name`` (``"mean"``, ``"sum"``, ...), or
    ``None`` if unknown: ``min``, ``max`` and ``mean`` are in the values'
    unit, ``sum`` in it times the weights', the moment sums ``m2`` ... ``m4``
    in its powers times the weights', the variances in its square and the
    standard deviations in it (a difference of degrees Celsius is in
    kelvin), ``skewness``, ``kurtosis`` and ``n`` pure numbers, ``weight``
    in the weights' unit."""
    from tack.dataset import units

    u, w = self.unit, self.weight_unit
    if name not in self._fields or name in ("unit", "weight_unit"):
        raise KeyError(f"no statistic {name!r}")
    if name in ("min", "max", "mean"):
        return u
    if name == "sum":
        return u if w == "dimensionless" else units.derived(u, w)
    if name in ("m2", "m3", "m4"):
        return units.derived((units.delta(u), int(name[1])), w)
    if name.endswith("variance"):
        return units.derived((units.delta(u), 2))
    if name.endswith("stddev"):
        return units.delta(u)
    if name == "weight":
        return w
    return "dimensionless"                   # n, skewness, kurtosis

docs.text:
entropy(data, field, bins=10, weights=None, level=None)

The Shannon entropy, in bits, of a scalar field's values in bins equal bins over their range: -sum(p log2 p) over the bins' shares, as Viskores' Entropy filter. Ghosts are left out: cells and points data.ghosts marks a duplicate or hidden.

Over a PartitionedDataSet, field names a field every piece has: the range is the whole's, and each piece's histogram over what it owns, made on its own device, is summed, over every rank of data.world. Over an AMRDataSet, the same over every box of every level, refined cells and points left out; over an OctreeDataSet, its leaves (or one level's nodes). With weights ("volume" or a field, as statistics takes them) each bin's share is the weights' sum in it over theirs.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/entropy.py 
@on_inputs_device
def entropy(data, field, bins=10, weights=None, level=None):
    """The Shannon entropy, in bits, of a scalar field's values in ``bins`` equal bins
    over their range: ``-sum(p log2 p)`` over the bins' shares, as Viskores'
    Entropy filter. Ghosts are left out: cells and points ``data.ghosts``
    marks a duplicate or hidden.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, ``field`` names a field every piece has: the
    range is the whole's, and each piece's histogram over what it owns, made on
    its own device, is summed, over every rank of ``data.world``. Over an
    ``AMRDataSet``, the same over every box of every level, refined cells and
    points left out; over an ``OctreeDataSet``, its leaves (or one ``level``'s
    nodes). With ``weights`` (``"volume"`` or a field, as ``statistics`` takes
    them) each bin's share is the weights' sum in it over theirs."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet
    from tack.dataset.octree import OctreeDataSet

    if isinstance(data, OctreeDataSet):
        return data._entropy(field, bins, weights, level)
    if level is not None:
        raise TypeError("level= picks an octree's level; this is not an OctreeDataSet")
    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        data = data._as_pieces()
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        fields_of(data, field, "entropy")
        extrema = [e for e in _over_pieces(data, lambda piece: _extrema(piece, field))
                   if e is not None]
        if not extrema:
            raise ValueError("entropy of no values")
        value_range = (float(np.min([e[0] for e in extrema])),
                       float(np.max([e[1] for e in extrema])))

        def counts(piece):
            if _extrema(piece, field) is None:
                return np.zeros(bins)
            return _counts(piece, field, bins, value_range, weights)
        p = sum(_over_pieces(data, counts))
    else:
        if _extrema(data, field) is None:
            raise ValueError("entropy of no values")
        # The histogram's own range, as before: it refuses one that is not finite.
        p = _counts(data, field, bins, None, weights)
    return _bits(p)
