def ghost_points(data, radius=None, k=None, periodic=None, around=None, fields=None,
                 world=None):
    """``data``'s pieces, point clouds (``point_cloud``: one vertex cell per point),
    each with copies of the other pieces' points it needs appended as ghosts: a
    new ``PartitionedDataSet``.

    With ``radius``, every point within ``radius`` of the piece's box: a filter
    over the points within ``radius`` (``outliers``' radius test,
    ``point_normals``, ``sph_density``, ``sph_interpolate`` with its kernel's
    reach) then gives each owned point the whole's answer. ``around`` (a
    ``PartitionedDataSet`` with a piece for each of ``data``'s) widens each
    piece's box to its own piece's points too: the targets ``sph_interpolate``
    resamples onto there. With ``k``, every point among an owned
    point's ``k`` nearest, wherever it is: ``point_normals`` and ``outliers``
    by the ``k`` nearest then see the whole's neighbours.

    Each copy is a vertex cell marked ``DUPLICATECELL`` at a point marked
    ``DUPLICATEPOINT``, owned by the piece it came from, after the piece's own
    points, which keep their order. Point and cell fields come along
    (``fields`` choosing, as filters do), sets keep their members, and global
    ids come along where every piece has them. ``update_ghosts`` refreshes a
    field's copies from their owners, after a per-piece filter that is right
    only on what a piece owns (``sph_density`` before ``sph_interpolate``).

    In a ``periodic`` box (as ``PointLocator`` takes it) a copy across a face is
    an image, moved by the box's side: run filters on the result without
    ``periodic``. ``data`` holds this rank's pieces, on any devices, in
    ``world`` (``data.world`` by default), on one origin, without ghosts."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "ghost_points' radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "ghost_points' periodic box")
    ghosted = _ghosted(data, radius, k, periodic, around, fields, world)
    result = PartitionedDataSet(ghosted.pieces, world=ghosted.blocks.world)
    result._ghost_plans = {"points": ghosted.plan, "cells": ghosted.plan}
    return result

update_ghosts(data, *fields)

Copy the named fields' values on ghost points and cells from the pieces that own them, in place, for a PartitionedDataSet that ghost_cells or ghost_points made.

A filter that needs each entity's neighbours -- project to points, point gradients -- is right on what a piece owns and wrong on the ghost layer's rim; refreshing the ghosts makes a second such filter right too. Each named field is a point or cell field of explicit values on every piece. One exchange moves all the point fields, one all the cell fields.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/ghost_cells.py 
def update_ghosts(data, *fields):
    """Copy the named fields' values on ghost points and cells from the pieces that
    own them, in place, for a ``PartitionedDataSet`` that ``ghost_cells`` or
    ``ghost_points`` made.

    A filter that needs each entity's neighbours -- ``project`` to points, point
    gradients -- is right on what a piece owns and wrong on the ghost layer's
    rim; refreshing the ghosts makes a second such filter right too. Each named
    field is a point or cell field of explicit values on every piece. One
    exchange moves all the point fields, one all the cell fields."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet

    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.amr_ghosts import amr_update_ghosts

        amr_update_ghosts(data, fields)
        return
    plans = getattr(data, "_ghost_plans", None)
    if plans is None:
        raise ValueError("update_ghosts needs the PartitionedDataSet ghost_cells or "
                         "ghost_points made, which keeps the exchanges")
    pieces = list(data)
    blocks = plans["points"].blocks
    by_kind = {"points": {g: {} for g in blocks.local}, "cells": {g: {} for g in blocks.local}}
    for name in fields:
        for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces):
            if name not in piece.fields:
                raise KeyError(f"partition {g - blocks.local.start} has no field {name!r}")
            field = piece.fields[name]
            kind = _kind(field)
            if kind is None:
                raise TypeError(f"update_ghosts refreshes point and cell fields; {name!r} "
                                f"is in {field.space!r}")
            if not isinstance(field.values, tack.Array):
                raise TypeError(f"update_ghosts writes the values in place; {name!r} holds "
                                f"a {type(field.values).__name__}, not a Tack array")
            by_kind[kind][g][name] = field.values
    for kind, values in by_kind.items():
        if any(values.values()):
            plans[kind].run(values)

remove_ghosts(data, fields=None)

data without its ghost cells -- the cells another piece owns (DUPLICATECELL) and the hidden ones (HIDDENCELL) -- and the points no remaining cell uses, as VTK's vtkRemoveGhosts: the last step before rendering, writing one file, or handing a piece to code that does not know ghost marks. Filters keep the ghost layers' output, which the next filter near a piece's edge needs, until this.

The points kept keep their marks: a point a piece shares with another is still that one's, so reductions still count it once. A point this piece owns stays even when only ghost cells used it (a point a filter made on an edge goes to the piece owning the edge's smallest point, whose cells there may all be ghosts), so every point keeps its one owner. A structured grid whose remaining cells are a block stays a structured grid; otherwise the cells are kept as extract_cells keeps them. data itself comes back when it has no ghost cells.

@on_inputs_device
def remove_ghosts(data, fields=None):
    """``data`` without its ghost cells -- the cells another piece owns
    (``DUPLICATECELL``) and the hidden ones (``HIDDENCELL``) -- and the points no
    remaining cell uses, as VTK's vtkRemoveGhosts: the last step before
    rendering, writing one file, or handing a piece to code that does not know
    ghost marks. Filters keep the ghost layers' output, which the next filter
    near a piece's edge needs, until this.

    The points kept keep their marks: a point a piece shares with another is
    still that one's, so reductions still count it once. A point this piece
    owns stays even when only ghost cells used it (a point a filter made on an
    edge goes to the piece owning the edge's smallest point, whose cells there
    may all be ghosts), so every point keeps its one owner. A structured grid
    whose remaining cells are a block stays a structured grid; otherwise the
    cells are kept as ``extract_cells`` keeps them. ``data`` itself comes back
    when it has no ghost cells."""
    if data._ghosts_lost:
        raise ValueError("this dataset is a filter's output that lost its input's ghost "
                         "marks, so which of its cells are ghosts is not known")
    ghosts = data.ghosts
    if ghosts is None or ghosts.cells is None:
        return data
    keep = tack.empty((data.num_cells,), tack.i32)
    if data.num_cells:
        _unmarked(ghosts.cells, Ghosts.SKIPPED_CELLS, keep)
    owned = None
    if ghosts.points is not None:
        owned = tack.empty((data.num_points,), tack.i32)
        if data.num_points:
            _unmarked(ghosts.points, Ghosts.DUPLICATEPOINT, owned)
    if isinstance(data.topology, StructuredTopology):
        block = _kept_block(data, keep, owned)
        if block is not None:
            return block
    return _keep_cells(data, keep, fields, keep_points=owned)

data's pieces numbered across every piece, as VTK's vtkGenerateGlobalIds: a new PartitionedDataSet of the same pieces with global_ids (tack.dataset.GlobalIds), every point and cell one id, the same on every piece holding it.

Each piece numbers what it owns in its own order, after the pieces before it -- piece 0's owned points from 0, then piece 1's -- and copies take their owner's ids. Owners come from the ghost marks where pieces have them (a copy marked DUPLICATEPOINT or DUPLICATECELL is another piece's); a point several pieces hold unmarked, as pieces without ghost cells share their boundary points, belongs to the lowest of them, and is marked DUPLICATEPOINT in the others, as VTK marks it. Points are copies of each other when their positions are exactly equal -- or, with tolerance, at most that far apart (in the spatial unit, or a quantity), chains of them too, for pieces whose copies of a shared point differ in their last bits -- and cells when their points' global ids are; pieces from ghost_cells reuse the exchanges it kept instead of matching again. Points a piece repeats within itself stay apart: merge_points merges them first.

data holds this rank's pieces, on any devices; world is the tack.communication.World they live in (data.world by default). The matching runs on the host and the exchanges on the pieces' devices.

def generate_global_ids(data, world=None, tolerance=0.0):
    """``data``'s pieces numbered across every piece, as VTK's
    ``vtkGenerateGlobalIds``: a new ``PartitionedDataSet`` of the same pieces with
    ``global_ids`` (``tack.dataset.GlobalIds``), every point and cell one id,
    the same on every piece holding it.

    Each piece numbers what it owns in its own order, after the pieces before
    it -- piece 0's owned points from 0, then piece 1's -- and copies take their
    owner's ids. Owners come from the ghost marks where pieces have them (a
    copy marked ``DUPLICATEPOINT`` or ``DUPLICATECELL`` is another piece's);
    a point several pieces hold unmarked, as pieces without ghost cells share
    their boundary points, belongs to the lowest of them, and is marked
    ``DUPLICATEPOINT`` in the others, as VTK marks it. Points are copies of
    each other when their positions are exactly equal -- or, with
    ``tolerance``, at most that far apart (in the spatial unit, or a
    quantity), chains of them too, for pieces whose copies of a shared point
    differ in their last bits -- and cells when their points' global ids are;
    pieces from ``ghost_cells`` reuse the exchanges it kept instead of
    matching again. Points a piece repeats within itself stay apart:
    ``merge_points`` merges them first.

    ``data`` holds this rank's pieces, on any devices; ``world`` is the
    ``tack.communication.World`` they live in (``data.world`` by default).
    The matching runs on the host and the exchanges on the pieces' devices.
    """
    if not isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"generate_global_ids takes a PartitionedDataSet, not "
                        f"{type(data).__name__}")
    world = data.world if world is None else world
    common_origin(data, "generate_global_ids", world)
    tolerance = _tolerance(data, tolerance, "generate_global_ids")
    pieces = list(data)
    blocks = tc.Blocks([piece.device for piece in pieces], world)
    plans = getattr(data, "_ghost_plans", None)
    marks = {g: _marks(piece) for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces)}

    # Points: who owns each, then the owners' numbers, then the copies'.
    if plans is not None:
        point_plan = plans["points"]
        point_owned = {g: (marks[g][1] & Ghosts.DUPLICATEPOINT) == 0 for g in blocks.local}
        point_shared = None
    else:
        point_owned, point_plan, point_shared = _point_owners(blocks, pieces, marks,
                                                                 tolerance)
    point_ids = _numbered(blocks, pieces, point_owned, point_plan, "points")

    # Cells: owned cells numbered, ghost cells from their owners.
    cell_owned = {g: (marks[g][0] & Ghosts.DUPLICATECELL) == 0 for g in blocks.local}
    copies = blocks.all_reduce({g: int((~cell_owned[g]).sum()) for g in blocks.local})
    if plans is not None:
        cell_plan = plans["cells"]
    elif copies:
        cell_plan = _cell_owners(blocks, pieces, marks, point_ids, point_shared)
    else:
        cell_plan = None
    cell_ids = _numbered(blocks, pieces, cell_owned, cell_plan, "cells")

    out = []
    for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces):
        points = marks[g][1] | np.where(point_owned[g], 0,
                                        Ghosts.DUPLICATEPOINT).astype(np.uint8)
        with blocks.device(g):
            ghosts = piece.ghosts
            if not np.array_equal(points, marks[g][1]):     # copies newly marked
                ghosts = Ghosts(cells=None if ghosts is None else ghosts.cells, points=points)
            copy = DataSet(piece.topology, piece.geometry, fields=dict(piece.fields),
                           sets=dict(piece.sets), dtype=piece.dtype, ghosts=ghosts,
                           global_ids=GlobalIds(cells=cell_ids[g], points=point_ids[g]),
                           **piece._frame())
        copy._ghosts_lost = piece._ghosts_lost
        out.append(copy)
    result = PartitionedDataSet(out, world=world)
    if plans is not None:
        result._ghost_plans = plans
    return result

data's pieces as one dataset: every cell a piece owns, once, and every point once, with the point and cell fields (fields choosing them as filters do), as VTK's vtkMergeBlocks after vtkRemoveGhosts.

Copies of a point several pieces hold become one point, matched as generate_global_ids matches them (the ghost marks' owners, else exact positions, or positions at most tolerance apart); ghost cells are left out, and hidden cells kept, marked. The points and cells are numbered as generate_global_ids numbers them: each piece's owned ones after the pieces before it. The pieces' own global ids, if they have them, come along as the result's.

Structured pieces that tile a box of cells (each placed by its topology.offset) give one structured grid of the box -- split's input back -- with its offset and its coordinates (uniform, rectilinear or explicit); other pieces give an unstructured dataset.

Across MPI ranks every rank passes its pieces and the result is on the root rank (None elsewhere), on device (by default the device of the root rank's first piece).

def merge_pieces(data, root=0, fields=None, device=None, tolerance=0.0):
    """``data``'s pieces as one dataset: every cell a piece owns, once, and every point
    once, with the point and cell fields (``fields`` choosing them as filters
    do), as VTK's vtkMergeBlocks after vtkRemoveGhosts.

    Copies of a point several pieces hold become one point, matched as
    ``generate_global_ids`` matches them (the ghost marks' owners, else exact
    positions, or positions at most ``tolerance`` apart); ghost cells are left out, and hidden cells kept, marked. The
    points and cells are numbered as ``generate_global_ids`` numbers them:
    each piece's owned ones after the pieces before it. The pieces' own global
    ids, if they have them, come along as the result's.

    Structured pieces that tile a box of cells (each placed by its
    ``topology.offset``) give one structured grid of the box -- ``split``'s
    input back -- with its offset and its coordinates (uniform, rectilinear
    or explicit); other pieces give an unstructured dataset.

    Across MPI ranks every rank passes its pieces and the result is on the
    ``root`` rank (``None`` elsewhere), on ``device`` (by default the device
    of the root rank's first piece)."""
    if not isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"merge_pieces takes a PartitionedDataSet, not {type(data).__name__}")
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.ghost_cells import _carried, _kind

    pieces = list(data)
    names = _carried(pieces, fields, "merge_pieces")
    common_origin(data, "merge_pieces")
    tolerance = _tolerance(data, tolerance, "merge_pieces")
    blocks = tc.Blocks([piece.device for piece in pieces], data.world)
    world = blocks.world
    if not 0 <= root < world.size:
        raise ValueError(f"root is a rank, 0 to {world.size - 1}, not {root}")
    firsts = blocks.all_gather({g: g == blocks.local.start for g in blocks.local})
    starts = [g for g, first in enumerate(firsts) if first]
    target = next((g for g in starts if blocks.rank_of(g) == root), None)
    if target is None:
        raise ValueError(f"merge_pieces gathers onto a piece of rank {root}, which has none")
    on_root = target in blocks.local
    out_device = (tack.device(device) if device is not None else
                  blocks.device(target)) if on_root else None
    structured = blocks.all_gather({g: isinstance(p.topology, StructuredTopology)
                                    for g, p in zip(blocks.local, pieces)})
    if all(structured):
        tiled = _box(blocks, pieces)
        if tiled is not None:
            return _merged_structured(blocks, pieces, names, _kind, target, out_device,
                                      tiled)
    return _merged_unstructured(blocks, pieces, names, _kind, target, out_device,
                                tolerance)

docs.text:
average_down(amr, field)

Put the finer levels' data into the coarse cells and points they cover, in place, as AMReX's average_down: each refined coarse cell (REFINEDCELL) takes the volume-weighted average of the fine cells over it, each refined coarse point (REFINEDPOINT) the value of the fine point at its location. field names a floating-point point or cell field every box has; finest level first, so a value reaches the coarsest level in one call.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/algorithms/amr_ghosts.py 
def average_down(amr, field):
    """Put the finer levels' data into the coarse cells and points they cover, in
    place, as AMReX's ``average_down``: each refined coarse cell (``REFINEDCELL``)
    takes the volume-weighted average of the fine cells over it, each refined
    coarse point (``REFINEDPOINT``) the value of the fine point at its location.
    ``field`` names a floating-point point or cell field every box has; finest
    level first, so a value reaches the coarsest level in one call."""
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.cell_geometry import cell_geometry
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.ghost_cells import _kind

    if not isinstance(amr, AMRDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"average_down takes an AMRDataSet, not {type(amr).__name__}")
    boxes = [box for _, box in amr]
    kinds = {_kind(box.fields[field]) for box in boxes}
    if len(kinds) != 1 or None in kinds:
        raise TypeError(f"average_down averages a point or cell field; {field!r} is not one")
    kind = kinds.pop()
    layout = _Layout(amr)
    d = amr.dimension
    for level in range(amr.num_levels - 2, -1, -1):
        rows = {}
        for g, (lv, k) in zip(layout.blocks.local, layout.local):
            rows[g] = _down_rows(amr, layout, lv, k, kind, d) if lv == level else \
                (_extent_size(amr._extents[lv][k], kind, d), np.zeros(0, np.int64), [])
        fill = _Fill(layout.blocks, rows)
        values = {g: box.fields[field].values for g, box in zip(layout.blocks.local, boxes)}
        for g, array in values.items():
            scalar = getattr(array.dtype, "scalar_dtype", array.dtype)
            if not isinstance(array, tack.Array) or scalar.numpy_dtype.kind != "f":
                raise TypeError(f"average_down averages floating-point values of explicit "
                                f"arrays; {field!r} is not one")
        if kind == "points":
            fill.run(values)
            continue
        # Cells: sums of measure times value over sums of measure.
        weighted, measures = {}, {}
        for g, box in zip(layout.blocks.local, boxes):
            with box.device:
                measures[g] = arrays.materialize(cell_geometry(box).measure.values)
                weighted[g] = _times(values[g], measures[g])
        fill.run(weighted)
        fill.run(measures)
        for g in layout.blocks.local:
            targets = fill.boxes[g]["targets"]
            if len(targets):
                with layout.blocks.device(g):
                    _divide(weighted[g], measures[g], tack.array(targets, tack.i64), values[g])

docs.title: tack.dataset.DataSet
docs.text:
DataSet(
    topology,
    geometry,
    fields=None,
    sets=None,
    dtype=None,
    ghosts=None,
    global_ids=None,
    origin=None,
    unit=None,
    time=None,
    time_unit=None,
)

A topology, a geometry, named fields and named sets. The geometry is a Field in H1 or L2 of 3-vectors -- or positions per point (a host array, or any array of 3-vectors, such as a device array or a CartesianProduct), which become an H1 field -- kept apart from fields as data.geometry: algorithms move it with the cells, never as one of the fields they carry or select. ghosts, a tack.dataset.Ghosts or None, marks the cells and points another piece of a partitioned dataset owns; global_ids, a tack.dataset.GlobalIds or None, numbers them across the pieces.

origin, three floats kept in double precision on the host, is where the geometry's coordinates start: a position is origin + value, the value in the geometry's type (tack.f32, or tack.f64 on a device that has it). Kernels see only the values, so coordinates far from zero -- a LiDAR survey's eastings and northings -- keep their precision in single precision. Filters keep it; what takes or gives absolute positions (implicit functions, probe points, seeds, world_positions, the VTK interop) converts on the host in double precision.

unit is the spatial unit, the geometry field's (DataSet.unit), in which origin is too; a geometry Field brings its own.

time is when the data are, a double on the host or None, in time_unit (a unit of time, or None for unknown): one step of a simulation as it streams through filters, which keep both, as they keep the origin. Tack holds no series of steps; filters that need earlier steps keep what they need (tack.dataset.temporal).

@on_inputs_device
def __init__(self, topology, geometry, fields=None, sets=None, dtype=None,
             ghosts=None, global_ids=None, origin=None, unit=None, time=None,
             time_unit=None):
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    self.topology = topology
    self._geometry = _as_geometry(geometry, topology, dtype, unit)
    self.origin = origin
    self.time = time
    self.time_unit = time_unit
    self.fields = dict(fields or {})
    for name, field in self.fields.items():
        if field.space.topology is not topology:
            raise ValueError(f"field {name!r} is on another topology")
    self.sets = sets
    # Set by a filter that dropped its input's ghost marks (ghosts.drop_marks).
    self._ghosts_lost = False
    self.ghosts = ghosts
    self.global_ids = global_ids
    _ = self._device                    # refuses parts on two devices

to_device(device)

def to_device(self, device):
    """This dataset on ``device``: itself if it is already there, else a copy --
    the topology made from its arrays copied there, each field in the same
    space on it, the sets by the same ids. What the topology derives (faces,
    groups, layouts) is derived there afresh, not copied."""
    from tack.dataset.sets import Set

    target = as_device(backend_of(device))
    here = self._device
    if here is not None and target._backend.memory_domain == here.memory_domain:
        return self
    topology = self.topology.to_device(target)

    def moved(field):
        space = field.space._rebuilt_on(topology)
        values = field.values.to_device(target)
        if isinstance(space, L2) and space.layout != field.space.layout:
            values = _relaid(values, field.space, space)      # "auto" chose another
        return Field(space, values, field.unit)

    sets = {name: Set._from_sorted_ids(topology, s.on, s.ids.to_device(target))
            for name, s in self.sets.items()}
    ghosts = None if self.ghosts is None else self.ghosts.to_device(target)
    global_ids = None if self.global_ids is None else self.global_ids.to_device(target)
    out = DataSet(topology, moved(self.geometry),
                  {name: moved(field) for name, field in self.fields.items()},
                  sets, dtype=self.dtype, ghosts=ghosts, global_ids=global_ids,
                  **self._frame())
    out._ghosts_lost = self._ghosts_lost
    return out

def positions(self):
    """Every point's position as a host array, ``(num_points, 3)``: an ``H1``
    geometry's values, relative to ``origin`` (``world_positions`` adds it).
    An ``L2`` geometry has none per point."""
    if isinstance(self.geometry.space, L2):
        raise ValueError("an L2 geometry has positions per cell corner, not per point")
    # An order-2 geometry's first values are the points'.
    return arrays.to_host(self.geometry.values)[:self.num_points]

rebased(origin)

This dataset with its geometry relative to origin instead: the same world positions, each value moved by the difference of the two origins (taken in double precision, added in the geometry's type). An image stays an image, its corner moved in double precision, so an image at survey coordinates rebased to a nearby origin holds its points exactly; a rectilinear grid moves its axes. Other implicit geometry becomes positions per point.

def rebased(self, origin):
    """This dataset with its geometry relative to ``origin`` instead: the same
    world positions, each value moved by the difference of the two origins
    (taken in double precision, added in the geometry's type). An image
    stays an image, its corner moved in double precision, so an image at
    survey coordinates rebased to a nearby origin holds its points exactly;
    a rectilinear grid moves its axes. Other implicit geometry becomes
    positions per point."""
    from tack.arrays import CartesianProduct, UniformCoordinates
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._moving import _moved, _shifted

    origin = as_origin(origin)
    if origin == self.origin:
        return self
    offset = np.asarray(self.origin) - np.asarray(origin)
    values = self.geometry.values
    if isinstance(values, UniformCoordinates):
        moved = UniformCoordinates(values.dims, np.asarray(values._origin) + offset,
                                   values._spacing,
                                   values._matrix if values.ORIENTED else None,
                                   dtype=values.dtype, device=self.device)
    elif isinstance(values, CartesianProduct):
        axes = [arrays.to_host(axis).astype(np.float64).reshape(-1) + offset[a]
                for a, axis in enumerate((values.xs, values.ys, values.zs))]
        moved = CartesianProduct(*axes, dtype=values.dtype, device=self.device)
    else:
        moved = _shifted(self, offset)
    out = _moved(self, moved)
    out.origin = origin
    return out

@on_inputs_device
def domain_groups(self, domain):
    """The ``DomainGroup``s of ``domain``: ``"cells"``, ``"faces"``, ``"edges"``, or
    the name of a cell, face or edge set in ``sets`` -- a cell set's as the
    cell groups' subgroups of its members."""
    kind = self._kind(domain)
    if domain == "cells":
        return self.topology.groups()
    if domain == "faces":
        return self.topology.faces().groups()
    if domain == "edges":
        return self.topology.edges().groups()
    if kind == "faces":
        return self.topology.faces().groups(self.sets[domain].ids)
    if kind == "edges":
        return self.topology.edges().groups(self.sets[domain].ids)
    return self.launch_groups(domain)

@on_inputs_device
def domain_view(self, domain, group, extra=(), **extra_attributes):
    """``group``'s view: kind, shape, geometry, and for cells their incidence when
    faces and edges have been derived; ``extra`` mixins and attributes last
    (a space's node mixins, ``node_views``)."""
    mixins = []
    kind = self._kind(domain)
    geometry, attributes = _geometry_parts(self, group, kind)
    mixins.extend(geometry)
    if kind == "cells" and issubclass(group.kind, views._CellsById):
        mixins.append(views._PolyhedralWalk)
        if group.shape is shapes.Polyhedron:
            mixins.append(views._PolyhedralLocation)
        elif group.shape is shapes.Polygon:
            mixins.append(views._PolygonLocation)
        elif group.shape is shapes.PolyLine:
            mixins.append(views._PolylineLocation)
    if (kind == "cells" and issubclass(group.kind, views._PolylineCells)
            and self.topology._faces is not None):
        mixins.append(views._PolylineIncidence)
        attributes.update(cell_faces=self.topology.cell_faces,
                          cell_face_sides=self.topology.cell_face_sides)
    if kind == "cells":
        # A subgroup's index(c) is its position in the topology's group, so
        # it shares that group's incidence.
        faces = self.topology._faces
        # The cells the faces were derived from: those of the top dimension.
        if faces is not None and group.root in getattr(faces, "group_starts", {}):
            mixins.extend((views._FaceIncidence, views._FaceWalk))
            attributes.update(side_face=faces.side_face, side_slot=faces.side_slot,
                              side_orientation=faces.side_orientation,
                              face_start=faces.group_starts[group.root])
        elif group.shape.NUM_FACES and not issubclass(group.kind, (views._CellsById,
                                                                   views._PolylineCells)):
            # A shape's faces walk from its tables alone, with no derived
            # faces: a fresh mesh's volumes need not sort them.
            mixins.append(views._FaceWalk)
        edges = self.topology._edges
        if edges is not None and group.shape.NUM_EDGES:
            mixins.append(views._EdgeIncidence)
            attributes.update(side_edge=edges.side_edge, side_sign=edges.side_sign,
                              edge_start=edges.group_starts[group.root])
    # A key that shapes the kernel -- a size bucket's cap -- brings its mixin.
    for key, value in group.keys.items():
        if hasattr(key, "domain_mixin"):
            mixins.append(key.domain_mixin(value))
    mixins.extend(extra)
    attributes.update(extra_attributes)
    return group.view(*mixins, **attributes)

docs.text:
node_views(space)

Views over space's nodes, each visited once: entity views -- points, edges, quad faces, cells -- whose node_count(i) nodes have node_dof(i, j), where the node's value is in space's values, and node_position(i, j), where the geometry puts it. for_each(kernel, data, space, ...) runs a kernel over them:

for i in nodes:
    for j in range(nodes.node_count(i)):
        values[nodes.node_dof(i, j)] = f(nodes.node_position(i, j))

H1's nodes are its points and, at order 2, its edges' middles, its quad faces' centers and its hexahedra's and quads' interiors; a shared node's position is the mean of its entity's points on a straight geometry, the geometry's own value there on one of the space's layout, and on a curved geometry of another order (tensor cells) its trace on the edge or face at the node. L2's are its cells' corners (order 1) or parametric centers (order 0), Constant's and values on cells' the parametric centers, values on points' the points. Shared nodes need positions per point: an L2 geometry has none, and is refused for them. On polyhedra, polygons and polylines only point nodes exist.

def node_views(self, space):
    """Views over ``space``'s nodes, each visited once: entity views -- points,
    edges, quad faces, cells -- whose ``node_count(i)`` nodes have
    ``node_dof(i, j)``, where the node's value is in ``space``'s values, and
    ``node_position(i, j)``, where the geometry puts it. ``for_each(kernel,
    data, space, ...)`` runs a kernel over them:

        for i in nodes:
            for j in range(nodes.node_count(i)):
                values[nodes.node_dof(i, j)] = f(nodes.node_position(i, j))

    ``H1``'s nodes are its points and, at order 2, its edges' middles, its
    quad faces' centers and its hexahedra's and quads' interiors; a shared
    node's position is the mean of its entity's points on a straight
    geometry, the geometry's own value there on one of the space's layout,
    and on a curved geometry of another order (tensor cells) its trace on
    the edge or face at the node. ``L2``'s
    are its cells' corners (order 1) or parametric centers (order 0),
    ``Constant``'s and values on cells' the parametric centers, values on
    points' the points. Shared nodes need positions per point: an ``L2``
    geometry has none, and is refused for them. On polyhedra, polygons and
    polylines only point nodes exist."""
    from tack.dataset.spaces import Values, reference_cells

    if space.topology is not self.topology:
        raise ValueError("a space of another topology")
    geometry = self.geometry
    point_nodes = ((isinstance(space, H1) and space.order == 1)
                   or (isinstance(space, Values) and space.on == "points"))
    shared = point_nodes or isinstance(space, H1)
    if shared and not isinstance(geometry.space, H1):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"the nodes of {space!r} are shared by cells, and an L2 geometry gives a "
            "shared node no single position")
    out = []
    if shared and self.num_points:
        group = views.DomainGroup(views._Points, shapes.Vertex, (self.num_points,),
                            self.num_points, 0)
        mixins, attributes = _geometry_parts(self, group, "points")
        out.append(group.view(*mixins, views._PointDof, views._MeanPosition, **attributes))
    if point_nodes:
        return out
    if isinstance(space, Values) and space.on not in ("points", "cells"):
        raise TypeError(f"values on {space.on} have no nodes to visit as such; "
                        f"for_each over {space.on!r} visits them")
    reference_cells(self.topology, f"the nodes of {space!r}")
    # Order 2 on a geometry curved to a higher order needs its traces too.
    if isinstance(space, H1) and (space.order > 2 or (space.order == 2 and (all(
            space._any_order(g.shape) for g in self.topology.groups() if g.count)
            or geometry.space.order > 2))):
        return out + self._tensor_nodes(space)
    if isinstance(space, H1):
        face_dofs, cell_dofs, _ = space._layout()
        curved = geometry.space.order == 2
        where = views._GeometryAtDof if curved else views._MeanPosition
        for group in self.topology.edges().groups():
            if group.count:
                out.append(self.domain_view("edges", group, (views._EdgeDof, where),
                                            node_edge_base=self.num_points))
        if space.basis == bases.SERENDIPITY:
            return out                       # no face centres or insides stored
        if any(g.count and g.shape.QUADRATIC_FACES for g in self.topology.groups()):
            for group in self.topology.faces().groups():
                if group.count and group.shape is shapes.Quad:
                    out.append(self.domain_view("faces", group, (views._FaceDof, where),
                                                node_face_dofs=face_dofs))
        for group in self.topology.groups():
            if group.count and group.shape.QUADRATIC_INTERIOR:
                out.append(self.domain_view("cells", group, (views._InteriorDof, where),
                                            node_cell_dofs=cell_dofs))
        return out
    groups = (self.launch_groups("cells", keys=(space,)) if space.varies
              else self.topology.groups())
    out += [view for _, view in self._cell_node_views(space, groups)]
    return out

@on_inputs_device
def launch_groups(self, domain, fields=(), keys=()):
    """The groups a kernel over ``domain`` launches once each, given the ``Field``s
    it reads: the domain's groups, each split by the keys of the spaces among
    ``fields`` that vary from cell to cell, and by any other ``keys`` -- objects
    that give each cell a key, as ``polyhedra.SizeBuckets`` does."""
    kind = self._kind(domain)
    members = self.sets[domain] if kind == "cells" and domain != "cells" else None
    groups = self.topology.groups() if members is not None else self.domain_groups(domain)
    spaces = [members] if members is not None else []
    for field in fields:
        if field.space.varies and field.space not in spaces:
            spaces.append(field.space)
    spaces.extend(k for k in keys if k not in spaces)
    if kind != "cells" or not spaces:
        return groups
    # A cell set splits the groups by membership, and keeps its members.
    return [sub for group in groups if group.count
            for sub in _subgroups(group, tuple(spaces))
            if members is None or sub.keys[members] == 1]

def uniform_grid(dims, origin=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), spacing=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), direction=None,
                 dtype=None, device=None, unit=None):
    """A dataset of ``dims`` points (one to three sizes) at ``origin + direction @
    (ijk * spacing)``: VTK's image data, Viskores' uniform data set. Nothing per
    point is stored (``UniformCoordinates``). A size of 1 adds no cells, in any
    position, and a grid with no axis of two points has none (``grid_topology``).
    ``origin`` and ``spacing`` take a value per size given (or three), and
    ``direction`` is 3 x 3 (2 x 2 for a 2D image). It is on ``device`` (by
    default the default device).

    The image's coordinates are in the geometry's type, so one far from zero
    -- a raster at survey coordinates -- loses digits in single precision:
    ``rebased(origin)`` keeps it an image with its corner relative to a nearby
    dataset origin, moved in double precision, as a point cloud's origin
    keeps its points. ``unit`` is the spatial unit (``DataSet.unit``), which
    ``origin`` and ``spacing`` are in."""
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    topology = grid_topology(dims, device=device)   # the sizes as given, before padding
    return DataSet(topology, UniformCoordinates(dims, origin, spacing, direction, dtype=dtype,
                                                device=device), unit=unit)

Host positions are taken relative to origin in double precision before they become dtype; without one, float64 positions far from zero for their box's width get its lower corner, rounded down to whole units (automatic_origin), so a LiDAR survey's eastings and northings keep their precision in single precision, and other positions get zero. dtype is tack.f32, or tack.f64 on a device that has it. def point_cloud(positions, fields=None, origin=None, dtype=None, device=None, unit=None,
                units=None):
    """A point cloud: a dataset of ``positions``, one vertex cell per point (types,
    offsets and connectivity implicit, stored nowhere), with ``fields`` (a dict of
    names to one value per point, scalars or rows of components) as point data.

    ``positions`` is an ``(n, 3)`` host array of world positions, or a Tack array
    of 3-vectors already relative to ``origin``. Host positions are taken
    relative to ``origin`` in double precision before they become ``dtype``;
    without one, float64 positions far from zero for their box's width get its
    lower corner, rounded down to whole units (``automatic_origin``), so a
    LiDAR survey's eastings and northings keep their precision in single
    precision, and other positions get zero. ``dtype`` is
    ``tack.f32``, or ``tack.f64`` on a device that has it. Floating-point fields
    become ``dtype`` too; integer fields (a LAS classification, intensities) keep
    their type. ``unit`` is the spatial unit (``DataSet.unit``), which ``origin``
    is in, and ``units`` maps field names to their units."""
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    from tack.dataset import ids
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._extract import _vertex_cells
    from tack.dataset.topology import UnstructuredTopology

    target = as_device(backend_of(device))
    if dtype not in target._backend.supported_dtypes:
        raise TypeError(f"the {target} device has no {dtype} arrays; a point cloud there "
                        f"takes positions of {tack.f32} relative to an origin")
    if isinstance(positions, tack.Array):
        n = int(positions.shape[0])
        local = positions
    else:
        world = np.asarray(positions, np.float64 if np.asarray(positions).dtype == np.float64
                           else None).reshape(-1, 3)
        n = len(world)
        if origin is None and world.dtype == np.float64 and n:
            origin = automatic_origin(world.min(axis=0), world.max(axis=0))
        local = world.astype(np.float64) - np.asarray(as_origin(origin))
    with target:
        topology = UnstructuredTopology(*_vertex_cells(n, ids.choose(None, n)), num_points=n)
        data = DataSet(topology, local, dtype=dtype, origin=origin, unit=unit)
        units = dict(units or {})
        unknown = set(units) - set(fields or {})
        if unknown:
            raise KeyError(f"units for fields not given: {', '.join(map(repr, sorted(unknown)))}")
        for name, values in (fields or {}).items():
            if not isinstance(values, tack.Array):
                host = np.asarray(values)
                if host.shape[:1] != (n,):
                    raise ValueError(f"field {name!r} has {host.shape[:1]} values for "
                                     f"{n} points")
                if host.dtype.kind == "f":
                    host = host.astype(dtype.numpy_dtype)
                width = host.shape[1] if host.ndim == 2 else None
                if width:
                    from tack.lang.types import from_numpy_dtype

                    values = tack.array(np.ascontiguousarray(host),
                                        tack.vec(width, from_numpy_dtype(host.dtype)))
                else:
                    values = tack.array(np.ascontiguousarray(host))
            data.fields[name] = Field(H1(data), values, units.get(name))
    return data

def wavelet(extent=10, spacing=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), maximum=255.0,
            frequency=(60.0, 30.0, 40.0), magnitude=(10.0, 18.0, 5.0),
            standard_deviation=0.5, dtype=None, device=None):
    """VTK's and Viskores' wavelet on the grid of point indices ``extent`` (``n``:
    -n to n on every axis, or ``x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1``), points at index times
    ``spacing``: ``maximum * exp(-|a|^2 / (2 sd^2))`` plus ``magnitude`` times
    sin, sin and cos of ``frequency * a``, where ``a`` is ``center`` minus the
    point, each axis divided by its extent's length. It is on ``device`` (by
    default the default device)."""
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    lo, hi = _extent(extent)
    s = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(spacing, float), (3,))
    data = uniform_grid([int(hi[d] - lo[d] + 1) for d in range(3)],
                        [lo[d] * s[d] for d in range(3)], s, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    n = data.num_points
    out = tack.empty((n,), dtype, device=data.device)
    scale = [1.0 / (hi[d] - lo[d]) if hi[d] > lo[d] else 1.0 for d in range(3)]
    _wavelet(out, int(hi[0] - lo[0] + 1), int(hi[1] - lo[1] + 1), *map(float, lo),
             *map(float, s), *map(float, center), *scale, *map(float, frequency),
             *map(float, magnitude), float(maximum),
             1.0 / (2.0 * standard_deviation * standard_deviation))
    data.fields["RTData"] = Field(H1(data), out)
    return data

def tangle(dims=(16, 16, 16), dtype=None, device=None):
    """Viskores' tangle on ``dims`` points per axis over [0, 1]^3: the quartic
    ``(x^4 - 5x^2 + y^4 - 5y^2 + z^4 - 5z^2 + 11.8) / 5 + 1/2`` of the point
    mapped to [-3, 3]^3, the point field ``tangle``. It is on ``device`` (by
    default the default device)."""
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    dims = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(dims, int), (3,))
    if (dims < 2).any():
        raise ValueError("tangle needs at least two points per axis")
    cells = dims - 1
    data = uniform_grid(dims, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 1.0 / cells, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    out = tack.empty((data.num_points,), dtype, device=data.device)
    _tangle(out, int(dims[0]), int(dims[1]), *map(float, cells))
    data.fields["tangle"] = Field(H1(data), out)
    return data

Each box has VTK's two cell fields: Gaussian-Pulse, amplitude * exp(-sum(((c - pulse_origin) / pulse_width)^2)) over the first dimension axes at each cell's centre c, and Centroid, the centres. An AMRDataSet, its refined cells and points marked.

def amr_gaussian_pulse(dimension=3, root_spacing=0.5, refinement_ratio=2,
                       pulse_origin=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), pulse_width=(0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
                       amplitude=0.0001, dtype=None, device=None):
    """A two-level AMR hierarchy with a Gaussian pulse, as VTK's
    ``vtkAMRGaussianPulseSource`` makes it: a root image of 6 x 6 (x 6) points from
    ``(-2, -2, 0)``, and two boxes refining parts of it by ``refinement_ratio``.

    Each box has VTK's two cell fields: ``Gaussian-Pulse``, ``amplitude *
    exp(-sum(((c - pulse_origin) / pulse_width)^2))`` over the first
    ``dimension`` axes at each cell's centre ``c``, and ``Centroid``, the
    centres. An ``AMRDataSet``, its refined cells and points marked."""
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet
    from tack.dataset.spaces import Constant

    if dimension not in (2, 3):
        raise ValueError(f"dimension is 2 or 3, not {dimension!r}")
    r = int(refinement_ratio)
    h = float(root_spacing)
    origin = np.array([-2.0, -2.0, 0.0])
    # VTK's patches, as point ranges of the root: x, y (and z) inclusive.
    patches = ([(0, 2), (0, 3), (0, 5)], [(3, 5), (2, 5), (0, 5)])

    def box(points, spacing, corner, offset):
        dims = tuple(points)[:dimension]
        grid = uniform_grid(dims, origin=tuple(corner)[:dimension],
                            spacing=(spacing,) * dimension, dtype=dtype, device=device)
        topology = type(grid.topology)(dims, id_dtype=grid.topology.id_dtype,
                                       device=device, offset=tuple(offset)[:dimension])
        centres = _cell_centres(dims, corner[:dimension], spacing)
        d = (centres - np.asarray(pulse_origin, np.float64)[:dimension]) / \
            np.asarray(pulse_width, np.float64)[:dimension]
        pulse = float(amplitude) * np.exp(-(d * d).sum(axis=1))
        full = np.zeros((len(centres), 3))
        full[:, :dimension] = centres
        from tack.dataset.dataset import DataSet

        out = DataSet(topology, grid.geometry.values, dtype=dtype)
        with out.device:
            out.fields["Gaussian-Pulse"] = Field(Constant(out), tack.array(
                pulse.astype(dtype.numpy_dtype)))
            out.fields["Centroid"] = Field(Constant(out), tack.array(
                full.astype(dtype.numpy_dtype), tack.vec3(dtype)))
        return out

    root = box((6, 6, 6), h, origin, (0, 0, 0))
    fine = []
    for patch in patches:
        lo = np.array([a for a, _ in patch])
        points = [r * (b - a) + 1 for a, b in patch]
        fine.append(box(points, h / r, origin + lo * h, lo * r))
    return AMRDataSet([[root], fine], ratios=[r])

AMRDataSet(levels, ratios=(), domain=None, world=None)

Levels of structured boxes, each level finer than the one before: a block-structured AMR hierarchy, as VTK's vtkOverlappingAMR and AMReX's.

levels holds this rank's boxes of each level, a PartitionedDataSet or a list of DataSets each. Every box has a StructuredTopology (all of one dimension) whose offset is its first cell's index in its level, and any structured geometry: an image, a rectilinear grid or a curvilinear grid. ratios[l] refines level l into l + 1: a whole number, or one per axis. domain is level 0's cell-index box (lo, hi), hi exclusive; by default its boxes' bounding box. world is where the other ranks' boxes are (tack.communication.World; the levels' own, else this process).

Refused when made: boxes of a level that overlap; a box of level l + 1 that, coarsened, is not within level l's boxes (proper nesting); image boxes of a level not on one lattice (one spacing, one origin, axis-aligned: VTK's model); boxes with ghost cells (DUPLICATECELL).

The boxes it holds are copies of those given with their marks computed (REFINEDCELL, REFINEDPOINT, siblings' DUPLICATEPOINT; other bits kept), sharing their topology, geometry and fields. Iterating over it gives (level, box) for this rank's boxes, coarsest level first.

def __init__(self, levels, ratios=(), domain=None, world=None):
    levels = list(levels)
    if not levels:
        raise ValueError("an AMRDataSet has at least one level")
    if world is None:
        world = next((lvl.world for lvl in levels if isinstance(lvl, PartitionedDataSet)),
                     None)
    if world is None:
        from tack.communication import World
        world = World()
    self.world = world
    given = [list(lvl) for lvl in levels]
    self.dimension = self._dimension(given)
    self.ratios = self._ratios(ratios, len(given))
    boxes, self._first = [], []
    for level, pieces in enumerate(given):
        mine = np.array([_box(piece, self.dimension) for piece in pieces],
                        np.int64).reshape(-1, 2, 3)
        every = world._allgather(mine)
        self._first.append(int(sum(len(part) for part in every[:world.rank])))
        boxes.append(np.concatenate(every).reshape(-1, 2, 3))
    self._boxes = boxes
    #: Each box's arrays' cell-index box: the box itself, or grown by ghost
    #: layers (``ghost_cells``).
    self._extents = [b.copy() for b in boxes]
    self.layers = 0
    self._fills = None
    self.domain = self._domain(domain)
    self._check(given)
    self.levels = tuple(PartitionedDataSet([self._marked(level, k, piece)
                                            for k, piece in enumerate(pieces)], world)
                        for level, pieces in enumerate(given))

A grid of octrees, Morton-sorted: VTK's vtkHyperTreeGrid with branching factor 2, as a linear octree.

roots is the grid of root cells, a dataset of a StructuredTopology over an image's or a rectilinear grid's coordinates, 2D or 3D (uniform_grid, rectilinear_grid); its cell t (x fastest) is tree t. tree, level and key give each node: its tree, its level (0 at the root) and its Morton key at that level (integer coordinates in the tree interleaved, x lowest). Every node's ancestors must be among the nodes. fields maps names to one value per node (cell data), in the order the nodes are given; mask (one per node, nonzero hides) becomes HIDDENCELL. The nodes are sorted in pre-order and the fields with them. world is where other ranks' trees are, for reductions: each rank holds whole trees. units maps field names to their units (tack.dataset.units); the spatial unit is the roots' (unit).

OctreeDataSet.from_cells makes one from cells' levels and positions, as a RAMSES reader gives them; tack.interop.vtk converts vtkHyperTreeGrids.

def __init__(self, roots, tree, level, key, fields=None, mask=None, world=None,
             units=None):
    from tack.dataset.topology import StructuredTopology

    if not isinstance(roots.topology, StructuredTopology) or \
            not isinstance(roots.geometry.values, (UniformCoordinates, CartesianProduct)):
        raise TypeError("an octree's roots are an image or a rectilinear grid")
    self.roots = roots
    self.dimension = len(roots.topology.point_dims)
    if self.dimension not in (2, 3):
        raise ValueError("an octree is 2D or 3D")
    if world is None:
        from tack.communication import World
        world = World()
    self.world = world
    tree = np.asarray(arrays.to_host(tree) if isinstance(tree, tack.Array) else tree,
                      np.int64).reshape(-1)
    level = np.asarray(arrays.to_host(level) if isinstance(level, tack.Array) else level,
                       np.int64).reshape(-1)
    key = np.asarray(arrays.to_host(key) if isinstance(key, tack.Array) else key,
                     np.uint64).reshape(-1)
    if not len(tree) == len(level) == len(key):
        raise ValueError("tree, level and key give each node: one of each per node")
    d = self.dimension
    if len(level) and (level.min() < 0 or level.max() > MAX_LEVEL[d]):
        raise ValueError(f"levels run from 0 to {MAX_LEVEL[d]} in {d}D")
    if len(tree) and (tree.min() < 0 or tree.max() >= roots.num_cells):
        raise ValueError(f"trees are the roots' cells, 0 to {roots.num_cells - 1}")
    if len(key) and (key >> (d * level).astype(np.uint64)).any():
        raise ValueError("a key holds dimension bits a level: one is too large for its "
                         "level")
    order = _preorder(tree, level, key, d)
    self._tree, self._level, self._key = tree[order], level[order], key[order]
    _check_ancestors(self._tree, self._level, self._key, d)
    leaf = _leaves(self._tree, self._level, self._key, d)
    marks = np.where(leaf, 0, Ghosts.REFINEDCELL).astype(np.uint8)
    if mask is not None:
        mask = np.asarray(arrays.to_host(mask) if isinstance(mask, tack.Array) else mask
                          ).reshape(-1)
        marks[np.asarray(mask[order] != 0)] |= Ghosts.HIDDENCELL
    device = roots.device
    with device:
        self.tree = tack.array(self._tree, tack.i64)
        self.level = tack.array(self._level.astype(np.int32), tack.i32)
        self.key = tack.array(self._key, tack.u64)
        self.marks = tack.array(marks, tack.u8)
    self.fields = {}
    for name, values in (fields or {}).items():
        self.fields[name] = _reordered(values, order, device, len(order), name)
    unknown = set(units or {}) - set(self.fields)
    if unknown:
        raise KeyError(f"units for fields not given: {', '.join(map(repr, sorted(unknown)))}")
    self.units = {name: _units.canonical(unit) for name, unit in (units or {}).items()}
    self._geometry = None
    self._carried_keys = None

    3-vectors (f64 where the device has it, else the roots' type), from the
    keys, made once."""

This rank's leaves as a DataSet of voxels (pixels in 2D), relative to origin: cell c is the c-th leaf in the nodes' order (np.flatnonzero(octree.is_leaf)[c]), with every field's value there as cell data, and hidden leaves HIDDENCELL. Corners that coincide are one point, found by sorting their indices on the finest level's lattice; hanging corners stay hanging, as the tree has them. Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/octree.py 
def leaves(self):
    """This rank's leaves as a ``DataSet`` of voxels (pixels in 2D), relative to
    ``origin``: cell ``c`` is the ``c``-th leaf in the nodes' order
    (``np.flatnonzero(octree.is_leaf)[c]``), with every field's value there as
    cell data, and hidden leaves ``HIDDENCELL``. Corners that coincide are one
    point, found by sorting their indices on the finest level's lattice;
    hanging corners stay hanging, as the tree has them. Every filter that
    reads cell data works on it (``threshold``, ``cell_centers``, ``probe``).

    Each rank gives its own trees' leaves; a corner on a face between two
    ranks' trees is a point on both, unmarked."""
    from tack.algorithms import argsort, gather, inclusive_scan
    from tack.dataset import ids, shapes
    from tack.dataset.dataset import DataSet, Field
    from tack.dataset.spaces import Constant
    from tack.dataset.topology import UnstructuredTopology, uniform_cells

    d = self.dimension
    is_leaf = self.is_leaf
    count = int(is_leaf.sum())
    corners = count << d
    finest = self.finest
    nx, ny, nz = ([n - 1 for n in self.roots.topology.point_dims] + [1])[:3]
    idt = ids.choose(None, corners)
    dtype = _compute_type(self.device, self.roots.dtype)
    with self.device:
        leaf = tack.array(np.flatnonzero(is_leaf).astype(np.int64), tack.i64)
        columns = [tack.empty((corners,), tack.i64) for _ in range(3)]
        if count:
            _leaf_corners(leaf, self.tree, self.level, self.key, nx, ny, d, finest,
                          *columns)
        # Sorted by z, then y, then x (stable sorts from the fastest axis), so
        # points come x fastest; the runs of equal corners are the points.
        order = argsort(columns[0], index_dtype=tack.i64) if corners else \
            tack.empty((0,), tack.i64)
        for column in columns[1:d]:
            if corners:
                order = gather(order, argsort(gather(column, order), index_dtype=tack.i64))
        si, sj, sk = (gather(c, order) for c in columns)
        flags = tack.empty((corners,), tack.i32)
        numbers = tack.empty((corners,), tack.i64)
        connectivity = tack.empty((corners,), idt)
        points = 0
        if corners:
            _run_starts(si, sj, sk, flags)
            points = int(inclusive_scan(flags, numbers, corners))
            _numbered(order, numbers, connectivity)
        axes, plane = self._axes(dtype)
        positions = tack.empty((points,), tack.vec3(self.roots.dtype))
        if points:
            _lattice_points(si, sj, sk, flags, numbers, *axes, nx, ny, nz, finest, d,
                            plane, 1.0, positions)
        types, offsets = uniform_cells(shapes.VOXEL if d == 3 else shapes.PIXEL, count,
                                       idt)
        topology = UnstructuredTopology(types, offsets, connectivity, num_points=points)
        fields = {name: Field(Constant(topology), gather(values, leaf),
                              self.units.get(name))
                  for name, values in self.fields.items()}
        marks = gather(self.marks, leaf)
        ghosts = None
        if count and (marks.numpy() & Ghosts.HIDDENCELL).any():
            hidden = marks.numpy() & Ghosts.HIDDENCELL
            ghosts = Ghosts(cells=tack.array(hidden.astype(np.uint8), tack.u8))
    return DataSet(topology, positions, fields=fields, dtype=self.roots.dtype,
                   ghosts=ghosts, **self._frame())

An octree of cells given by their level and position (an (n, 3) world position inside each cell, its centre say), as a RAMSES reader or yt gives them -- whole octs: every refined cell's children. Each cell's tree is the root cell holding the position; its key, the integer coordinates there at its level. Ancestors no cell gives are added, their fields NaN (integer fields 0): reductions of the leaves never read them.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/octree.py 
@classmethod
def from_cells(cls, roots, level, position, fields=None, world=None, units=None):
    """An octree of cells given by their ``level`` and ``position`` (an ``(n, 3)``
    world position inside each cell, its centre say), as a RAMSES reader or
    yt gives them -- whole octs: every refined cell's children. Each cell's
    tree is the root cell holding the position; its key, the integer
    coordinates there at its level. Ancestors no cell gives are added, their
    fields NaN (integer fields 0): reductions of the leaves never read
    them."""
    level = np.asarray(level, np.int64).reshape(-1)
    position = np.asarray(position, np.float64).reshape(-1, 3) - np.asarray(roots.origin)
    d = len(roots.topology.point_dims)
    axes = _root_axes(roots)
    tree = np.zeros(len(level), np.int64)
    stride = 1
    index = np.zeros((len(level), 3), np.int64)
    for a in range(d):
        edges = axes[a]
        cell = np.clip(np.searchsorted(edges, position[:, a], side="right") - 1, 0,
                       len(edges) - 2)
        tree += cell * stride
        stride *= len(edges) - 1
        fraction = (position[:, a] - edges[cell]) / (edges[cell + 1] - edges[cell])
        index[:, a] = np.clip(np.floor(fraction * (1 << level)), 0,
                              (1 << level) - 1).astype(np.int64)
    key = _interleave(index, d)
    tree, level, key, fields = _with_ancestors(tree, level, key, fields or {}, d)
    return cls(roots, tree, level, key, fields=fields, world=world, units=units)

def __init__(self, point_dims, id_dtype=None, device=None, offset=None):
    point_dims = tuple(int(d) for d in point_dims)
    if not 1 <= len(point_dims) <= 3 or min(point_dims) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"point_dims must be 1 to 3 sizes of at least 2, not {point_dims}")
    offset = (0,) * len(point_dims) if offset is None else tuple(int(o) for o in offset)
    if len(offset) != len(point_dims):
        raise ValueError(f"offset needs one index per axis ({len(point_dims)}), not "
                         f"{offset}")
    self.point_dims = point_dims
    self.offset = offset
    self.num_cells = int(np.prod([d - 1 for d in point_dims]))
    self.num_points = int(np.prod(point_dims))
    self.id_dtype = ids.choose(id_dtype, max(self.num_points, 12 * self.num_cells))
    kind, shape = self._KINDS[len(point_dims)]
    dims = point_dims + (1,) * (3 - len(point_dims))
    # One group, kept: derived incidence is laid out per group.
    self._groups = [DomainGroup(kind, shape, (*dims, self.num_cells), self.num_cells, 0)]
    # It holds no arrays, so its device is the one it is made for: ``device``,
    # or the default device when it is made.
    self._found_device = backend_of(device)

def __init__(self, types, offsets, connectivity, num_points=None, id_dtype=None):
    self.types = _as_field(types, tack.u8)
    self.num_cells = size_of(self.types)
    offsets, connectivity = (v if isinstance(v, _Implicit) else ids.host_or_field(v)
                             for v in (offsets, connectivity))

        raise ValueError(f"offsets must have num_cells + 1 = {self.num_cells + 1} "
                         f"entries, not {size_of(offsets)}")

                else connectivity)
        num_points = int(used.max()) + 1 if used.size else 0
    self.num_points = int(num_points)
    extent = max(self.num_points, size_of(connectivity), 12 * self.num_cells)
    if id_dtype is None and any(isinstance(v, _Implicit) and v.dtype == tack.i64
                                for v in (offsets, connectivity)):
        id_dtype = tack.i64
    self.id_dtype = ids.choose(id_dtype, extent,

                                      if isinstance(v, Array)])
    self.offsets = _ids_of(offsets, self.id_dtype)
    self.connectivity = _ids_of(connectivity, self.id_dtype)
    self._groups = None
    if _checks_ids():

docs.title: tack.dataset.polyhedra
docs.text:
Polyhedral topologies: every cell a list of faces, every face a polygon stored once.

docs/vis-guide/design/polyhedra.md, phase 1. A PolyhedralTopology holds

  • face_offsets/face_points: each face's points (CSR), in the order that winds the face out of its side 0 -- the cell its normal points away from;
  • cell_offsets/cell_faces: each cell's faces (CSR);
  • cell_face_sides: one u8 per cell -> face entry, 0 if the face is wound out of that cell (it is the face's side 0), 1 if into it. This is the shape path's side_slot under the same meaning.

Face numbering is the input's: a producer's face ids (an MPAS edge id) are the face ids, so face data lines up with the file, and nothing re-derives them. Everything else is derived on demand by sorting, and kept:

  • faces(): the shape path's two-sided record per face, [cell0, local0, cell1, local1] (-1, -1 for a missing side 1), and the boundary;
  • cell_points(): each cell's points, its face points sorted and unique -- exactly what VTK keeps as a polyhedron's connectivity;
  • edges(): the faces' consecutive point pairs as (low, high) keys, sorted into runs -- the same numbering the shape path gives the same edges.

Ids are the topology's id_dtype (tack.dataset.ids), as on the shape path.

Orientation comes from the input, never from geometry. check_winding lists the cells that do not walk each of their edges once in each direction; orient turns a face wound into its only cell around. as_polyhedra converts any shape-based dataset, reusing its derived faces as they stand.

def __init__(self, face_offsets, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces, cell_face_sides,
             num_points=None, id_dtype=None):
    face_offsets, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces = (
        _given(a) for a in (face_offsets, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces))
    if num_points is None:
        num_points = _points_used(face_points)
    # Cell points and directed edges hold each face's points once per side.
    extent = max(int(num_points), 2 * size_of(face_points),
                 2 * size_of(face_offsets), size_of(cell_faces))
    given = (face_offsets, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces)
    self.id_dtype = idt = ids.choose(id_dtype, extent, given)
    self.face_offsets = _ids_of(face_offsets, idt)
    self.face_points = _ids_of(face_points, idt)
    self.cell_offsets = _ids_of(cell_offsets, idt)
    self.cell_faces = _ids_of(cell_faces, idt)
    self.cell_face_sides = _as_field(cell_face_sides, tack.u8)
    self.num_faces = size_of(self.face_offsets) - 1
    self.num_cells = size_of(self.cell_offsets) - 1
    if self.num_faces < 0 or self.num_cells < 0:
        raise ValueError("offsets have one entry more than there are faces or cells")
    if size_of(self.cell_face_sides) != size_of(self.cell_faces):
        raise ValueError("cell_face_sides needs one entry per cell_faces entry")
    self.num_points = int(num_points)
    self._cell_points = None
    self._groups = None
    if _checks_ids():
        _refuse("polyhedral topology", self._id_problems())

A topology from each cell's own list of faces (point-id rings), as VTK and many readers give them: copies of a face are matched by point set, the first copy found is the face -- its cell side 0 -- and a second copy, run the other way, is side 1. Two copies run the same way are refused.

With orient, the copies are made consistent first, on the host: within each cell, faces walk each shared edge in opposite directions; across cells, the two copies of a shared face run opposite ways (whole cells are reversed to make it so); then each connected component is turned outward as a whole, by the sign of its total volume -- the one geometric test, made once per component on a sum over many cells, which thin cells cannot fool as they fool a per-cell test. positions (one row per point) are needed for that last step.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/dataset/polyhedra.py 
@classmethod
def from_cell_faces(cls, cells, num_points, positions=None, orient=False, id_dtype=None):
    """A topology from each cell's own list of faces (point-id rings), as VTK and many
    readers give them: copies of a face are matched by point set, the first copy
    found is the face -- its cell side 0 -- and a second copy, run the other way,
    is side 1. Two copies run the same way are refused.

    With ``orient``, the copies are made consistent first, on the host:
    within each cell, faces walk each shared edge in opposite directions;
    across cells, the two copies of a shared face run opposite ways (whole
    cells are reversed to make it so); then each connected component is
    turned outward as a whole, by the sign of its total volume -- the one
    geometric test, made once per component on a sum over many cells, which
    thin cells cannot fool as they fool a per-cell test. ``positions`` (one
    row per point) are needed for that last step.
    """
    cells = [[[int(p) for p in ring] for ring in faces] for faces in cells]
    if orient:
        if positions is None:
            raise ValueError("orient needs the points' positions, for the sign of each "
                             "component's volume")
        cells = _orient_cells(cells, np.asarray(positions, float))
    rings = [ring for faces in cells for ring in faces]
    cell_offsets = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum([len(faces) for faces in cells])])
    ring_offsets = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum([len(ring) for ring in rings])])
    ring_points = np.fromiter((p for ring in rings for p in ring), np.int64,
                              int(ring_offsets[-1]))
    return cls._from_rings(cell_offsets, ring_offsets, ring_points, num_points,
                           id_dtype=id_dtype)

Polygons of any number of points, the polyhedral topology one dimension down: cells are polygons, their facets edges.

Built from point loops -- loop_points[loop_offsets[c]:loop_offsets[c + 1]] is polygon c's points in order -- as producers and isosurfaces give them. Facet k of a polygon is its edge from loop point k to the next. Edges are matched by sorting: the first polygon to use an edge is its side 0 and the edge runs its way; a second must run it the other way, or the winding is inconsistent (or the surface not orientable) and is refused, as is an edge of three polygons. loops() gives the loops back.

@on_inputs_device
def __init__(self, loop_offsets, loop_points, num_points=None, id_dtype=None):
    loop_offsets, loop_points = _given(loop_offsets), _given(loop_points)
    total = size_of(loop_points)
    if num_points is None:
        num_points = _points_used(loop_points)
    # Its facets' points are two per edge, and there are as many edges as loop points.
    idt = ids.choose(id_dtype, max(int(num_points), 4 * total + 2),
                     given=(loop_offsets, loop_points))
    loop_offsets = _ids_of(loop_offsets, idt)
    loop_points = _ids_of(loop_points, idt)
    if _checks_ids():
        # Before the facets are derived from the loops, which index by point.
        _refuse("polygonal topology", _csr_problems(
            loop_offsets, loop_points, int(num_points), "loop_offsets", "loop_points",
            "num_points"))
    n = size_of(loop_offsets) - 1
    keys = tack.empty((total,), tack.vec(2, idt))
    directions = tack.empty((total,), tack.i32)
    cell_faces = tack.empty((total,), idt)
    sides = tack.empty((total,), tack.u8)
    count = 0
    if total:
        _loop_edge_keys(loop_offsets, loop_points, keys, directions, n)
        order = key_order(keys, num_points, idt)
        offsets, count = run_offsets(keys, order)
    face_points = tack.empty((2 * count,), idt)
    if count:
        problems = tack.zeros((2,), tack.i32)
        _facets_from_runs(order, offsets, keys, directions, face_points, cell_faces,
                          sides, problems, count)
        if problems[0]:
            raise ValueError(f"{problems[0]} edges are shared by more than two polygons")
        if problems[1]:
            raise ValueError(f"{problems[1]} edges are walked the same way by both their "
                             "polygons: the winding is inconsistent, or the surface is "
                             "not orientable")
    face_offsets = tack.empty((count + 1,), idt)
    _every_other(face_offsets)
    super().__init__(face_offsets, face_points, loop_offsets, cell_faces, sides,
                     num_points=num_points, id_dtype=idt)
    self.loop_offsets = loop_offsets
    self.loop_points = loop_points

Polylines of any number of points, the polyhedral topology two dimensions down: each cell a chain of points, line_points[line_offsets[c]:line_offsets[c + 1]], two or more, as streamlines and VTK's VTK_POLY_LINE give them.

Its facets (faces(), codimension 1) are the chains' ends: a facet per point where chains end, its normal along the chain out of its side 0 -- the first chain ending there, in cell order -- and into its side 1, the second. A vertex has no winding, so any two chains meeting end to end are consistent. Three or more ending at one point (a branch) the faces cannot hold, and faces() refuses them, as an edge of three polygons is refused; the topology itself, and everything that does not need its faces, works. A chain may close (its last point its first): its two ends are then one interior facet. lines() gives the chains back; a cell's points (cell_points()) are its chain's, sorted and unique.

@on_inputs_device
def faces(self):
    """The chains' ends as faces (``PolygonFaces`` of one-point faces), derived on
    first use and kept; refuses a point where more than two chains end."""
    if self._faces is None:
        n, idt = self.num_cells, self.id_dtype
        cell_faces = tack.empty((2 * n,), idt)
        sides = tack.empty((2 * n,), tack.u8)
        count = 0
        if n:
            order = key_order(self._ends, self.num_points, idt)
            offsets, count = run_offsets(self._ends, order)
        face_points = tack.empty((count,), idt)
        if count:
            crowded = tack.zeros((1,), tack.i32)
            _ends_from_runs(order, offsets, self._ends, face_points, cell_faces, sides,
                            crowded, count)
            if crowded[0]:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"more than two polylines end at {crowded[0]} points: the faces of a "
                    "branching network are not defined (split it at the branches)")
        self.face_offsets = tack.empty((count + 1,), idt)
        _counting(self.face_offsets)
        self.face_points = face_points
        self.cell_offsets = tack.empty((n + 1,), idt)
        _every_other(self.cell_offsets)
        self.cell_faces = cell_faces
        self.cell_face_sides = sides
        self.num_faces = count
        self._faces = PolygonFaces(self)
    return self._faces
