    Raises:
        ValueError: if n_components contradicts the array's shape, does not
            divide its size, or the array has more than 2 dimensions.
    """
    # Work out the layout before reaching for VTK, so a shape mistake
    # reports itself rather than being masked by a missing-VTK error.
    if getattr(array, 'layout', 'aos') == 'soa':
        raise TypeError(
            "array_to_vtk() shares one buffer with VTK, and an SOA array has one per "
            "component; share each of its components, or copy it to one buffer with "
            "tack.array(a, layout='aos')")
    if hasattr(array, '_vector_n'):
        width = array._vector_n
        if n_components is not None and n_components != width:
            raise ValueError(
                f"n_components={n_components} contradicts the element width {width}")
        if len(array.shape) > 1:
            raise ValueError("reshape a typed array to one array dimension for VTK tuples")
        array = array._scalar_view().reshape((array.size, width))
        n_components = width
    ndim = len(array.shape)

    if n_components is None:
        if ndim == 2:
            n_components = array.shape[1]
        elif ndim <= 1:
            n_components = 1
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"a {ndim}-dimensional array has no obvious VTK layout; "
                f"reshape it to (tuples, components), or pass n_components "
                f"if it holds flat interleaved data")
    else:
        if n_components < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"n_components must be at least 1, got {n_components}")
        if ndim == 2 and array.shape[1] != n_components:
            raise ValueError(
                f"n_components={n_components} contradicts the array's shape "
                f"{array.shape}, which already says {array.shape[1]}")
        if array.size % n_components:
            raise ValueError(
                f"an array of {array.size} values does not divide into tuples "
                f"of {n_components}")

    dlpack_support = _dlpack_support()
    _require_shared_level_zero_context(dlpack_support, array._backend)

    # VTK reads the tensor as (tuples, components), so give it that shape.
    shaped = array
    if array.shape != (array.size // n_components, n_components):
        shaped = array.reshape((array.size // n_components, n_components))

    return dlpack_support.dlpack_to_vtk(shaped, name=name)

vtk_to_dataset(
    grid,
    dtype=_DEFAULT_FLOAT,
    polyhedral=None,
    orient=False,
    id_dtype=None,
    origin=None,
    copy=True,
)

Copy a vtkUnstructuredGrid, vtkPolyData, vtkStructuredGrid, vtkRectilinearGrid or vtkImageData into a tack.dataset.DataSet: an image's points as UniformCoordinates (with its direction matrix), a rectilinear grid's as a CartesianProduct, a structured grid's as its explicit points.

Points and floating-point arrays become fields of dtype, by default the default float type (tack.get_default_float(), f32 unless set); integer arrays keep their type. Named point data become H1 fields and named cell data Constant fields (a cell array named as a point array is "<name> (cells)", with a warning); a vtkGhostType array becomes the ghost marks (data.ghosts), not a field; a constant or affine array (VTK's implicit arrays) stays implicit, as a ConstantArray or CountingArray. An unstructured grid's cells must all be linear shapes -- or all VTK Lagrange curves, quadrilaterals or hexahedra of one order p, which become linear cells on their corner points, with the geometry and point data in H1(order=p, basis="equispaced") (VTK's Lagrange nodes) -- unless it holds polyhedra (or polyhedral is true), when it becomes a PolyhedralTopology, every cell a polyhedron of its faces, polylines, when it becomes a PolylineTopology (its lines two-point polylines, and no other cells allowed), or polygons (VTK_POLYGON), when it becomes a PolygonalTopology (its triangles and quads polygons too, and no other cells allowed). Its types, offsets and connectivity stay implicit where VTK's are (a cell type given as a number, affine offsets). Hexahedra with corners repeated as finite-element files write other shapes (Tecplot's bricks, degenerate Exodus and Patran hexahedra) become those shapes: a wedge [a, b, c, c, d, e, f, f] (in any rotation), a pyramid [a, b, c, d, e, e, e, e], a tetrahedron [a, b, c, c, d, d, d, d]. A vtkPolyData is taken as the unstructured grid of its cells in VTK's order -- verts (a poly vertex as its vertices), lines, polygons (of three or four points triangles and quads), and triangle strips, each strip as its triangles, which take its cell data -- so the same rules hold: a surface of triangles and quads is an UnstructuredTopology, one with larger polygons a PolygonalTopology, lines a PolylineTopology, and polylines or polygons beside other cells are refused. With orient, inconsistently wound polyhedra are repaired first (PolyhedralTopology.from_cell_faces); without it they are refused. VTK's ids are 64-bit; the topology keeps them in id_dtype, by default i32 unless the grid is too large for it (tack.dataset.ids).

origin (three numbers) becomes the dataset's origin: VTK's points, an image's origin and a rectilinear grid's lines are taken relative to it, subtracted in double precision before they become dtype, so points far from zero keep their precision. Without one, converting to f32 takes the lower corner of VTK's bounds, rounded down, where the data are more than 100 times farther from zero than they are wide (tack.dataset.dataset.automatic_origin; a composite's pieces one origin), and zero otherwise.

A vtkOverlappingAMR becomes an AMRDataSet: each block (an image or a rectilinear grid) converted as above, placed in its level by its vtkAMRBox, the levels' refinement ratios kept; the refined cells are marked afresh (VTK's vtkGhostType bits come in and are recomputed). Blocks with ghost layers are refused.

A vtkCellGrid (VTK's discontinuous-Galerkin cells, read from .dg files by vtkCellGridReader) becomes a DataSet of its cells on its shape attribute's corners: C1 attributes copied (shared ones as H1, per-cell ones as L2), constant ones as Constant, and every other HGRAD or Bezier basis resampled by VTK onto Tack's equispaced space of its order (tack.interop.vtk._cellgrid); HCURL and HDIV are left out, with a warning. It needs VTK's cell-type accessors on vtkCellAttribute, newer than 9.7.1.

A vtkPartitionedDataSet becomes a PartitionedDataSet, each piece converted as above (null pieces skipped), and a vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection a dict of them, keyed by each partitioned dataset's vtkCompositeDataSet.NAME() ("block<i>" where it has none, "<name>#<i>" for a name already taken).

VTK's DATA_TIME_STEP becomes the step's time (time), its unit unknown.

dtype=None keeps each floating-point array in its own type (f32 or f64), the points too; an image's geometry is then f64, as VTK's is. On a default device without f64 (Metal), it is f32, which such a device's arrays take.

With copy=False the dataset shares VTK's memory instead of copying it, as CPU arrays (whatever the default device): the points, data arrays, cell types, offsets and connectivity, ghost marks and global ids, wherever their values are one contiguous block of the type Tack keeps them in, and a polygonal dataset's cells where it holds one kind (verts, lines or polygons). Ids then keep VTK's width (id_dtype follows it unless given), and floating-point arrays are shared at their own precision with dtype=None. The shared arrays are read-only to Tack and hold VTK's arrays alive; what VTK changes in them afterwards, Tack sees. What cannot be shared -- an origin to subtract, a type to convert, triangle strips, collapsed hexahedra, polyhedra -- is copied as before.

With Metal the default device, copy=False gives Metal arrays instead, as Apple silicon's unified memory allows with any VTK: the buffers a Metal dataset handed VTK (dataset_to_vtk(copy=False)) come back as themselves, memory on whole pages is wrapped in place, and anything else is copied to Metal, so the dataset is on Metal throughout.

def vtk_to_dataset(grid, dtype=_DEFAULT_FLOAT, polyhedral=None, orient=False, id_dtype=None,
                   origin=None, copy=True):
    """Copy a ``vtkUnstructuredGrid``, ``vtkPolyData``, ``vtkStructuredGrid``,
    ``vtkRectilinearGrid`` or ``vtkImageData`` into a ``tack.dataset.DataSet``: an image's points as
    ``UniformCoordinates`` (with its direction matrix), a rectilinear grid's as a
    ``CartesianProduct``, a structured grid's as its explicit points.

    Points and floating-point arrays become fields of ``dtype``, by default the
    default float type (``tack.get_default_float()``, f32 unless set); integer
    arrays keep their type. Named point data become ``H1`` fields and named
    cell data ``Constant`` fields (a cell array named as a point array is
    ``"<name> (cells)"``, with a warning); a ``vtkGhostType`` array becomes the ghost marks
    (``data.ghosts``), not a field; a constant or affine array (VTK's implicit
    arrays) stays implicit, as a ``ConstantArray`` or ``CountingArray``. An
    unstructured grid's cells must all be linear shapes -- or all VTK Lagrange
    curves, quadrilaterals or hexahedra of one order ``p``, which become linear
    cells on their corner points, with the geometry and point data in
    ``H1(order=p, basis="equispaced")`` (VTK's Lagrange nodes) -- unless it holds
    polyhedra (or ``polyhedral`` is true), when it becomes a
    ``PolyhedralTopology``, every cell a polyhedron of its faces, polylines,
    when it becomes a ``PolylineTopology`` (its lines two-point polylines, and
    no other cells allowed), or polygons (``VTK_POLYGON``), when it becomes a
    ``PolygonalTopology`` (its triangles and quads polygons too, and no other
    cells allowed). Its types, offsets and connectivity stay implicit where
    VTK's are (a cell type given as a number, affine offsets). Hexahedra with
    corners repeated as finite-element files write other shapes (Tecplot's
    bricks, degenerate Exodus and Patran hexahedra) become those shapes: a
    wedge ``[a, b, c, c, d, e, f, f]`` (in any rotation), a pyramid ``[a, b, c,
    d, e, e, e, e]``, a tetrahedron ``[a, b, c, c, d, d, d, d]``.
    A ``vtkPolyData`` is taken as the unstructured grid of its cells in VTK's
    order -- verts (a poly vertex as its vertices), lines, polygons (of three or
    four points triangles and quads), and triangle strips, each strip as its
    triangles, which take its cell data -- so the same rules hold: a surface of triangles and quads is
    an ``UnstructuredTopology``, one with larger polygons a ``PolygonalTopology``,
    lines a ``PolylineTopology``, and polylines or polygons beside other cells
    are refused.
    With ``orient``, inconsistently wound polyhedra are repaired first
    (``PolyhedralTopology.from_cell_faces``); without it they are refused.
    VTK's ids are 64-bit; the topology keeps them in ``id_dtype``, by default
    ``i32`` unless the grid is too large for it (``tack.dataset.ids``).

    ``origin`` (three numbers) becomes the dataset's ``origin``: VTK's points,
    an image's origin and a rectilinear grid's lines are taken relative to it,
    subtracted in double precision before they become ``dtype``, so points far
    from zero keep their precision. Without one, converting to ``f32`` takes
    the lower corner of VTK's bounds, rounded down, where the data are more
    than 100 times farther from zero than they are wide
    (``tack.dataset.dataset.automatic_origin``; a composite's pieces one
    origin), and zero otherwise.

    A ``vtkOverlappingAMR`` becomes an ``AMRDataSet``: each block (an image or a
    rectilinear grid) converted as above, placed in its level by its
    ``vtkAMRBox``, the levels' refinement ratios kept; the refined cells are
    marked afresh (VTK's ``vtkGhostType`` bits come in and are recomputed).
    Blocks with ghost layers are refused.

    A ``vtkCellGrid`` (VTK's discontinuous-Galerkin cells, read from ``.dg``
    files by ``vtkCellGridReader``) becomes a ``DataSet`` of its cells on its
    shape attribute's corners: ``C1`` attributes copied (shared ones as ``H1``,
    per-cell ones as ``L2``), ``constant`` ones as ``Constant``, and every other
    ``HGRAD`` or Bezier basis resampled by VTK onto Tack's equispaced space of
    its order (``tack.interop.vtk._cellgrid``); ``HCURL`` and ``HDIV`` are left
    out, with a warning. It needs VTK's cell-type accessors on
    ``vtkCellAttribute``, newer than 9.7.1.

    A ``vtkPartitionedDataSet`` becomes a ``PartitionedDataSet``, each piece
    converted as above (null pieces skipped), and a
    ``vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection`` a ``dict`` of them, keyed by each
    partitioned dataset's ``vtkCompositeDataSet.NAME()`` (``"block<i>"`` where
    it has none, ``"<name>#<i>"`` for a name already taken).

    VTK's ``DATA_TIME_STEP`` becomes the step's time (``time``), its unit
    unknown.

    ``dtype=None`` keeps each floating-point array in its own type (f32 or f64),
    the points too; an image's geometry is then f64, as VTK's is. On a default
    device without f64 (Metal), it is f32, which such a device's arrays take.

    With ``copy=False`` the dataset shares VTK's memory instead of copying it,
    as CPU arrays (whatever the default device): the points, data arrays, cell
    types, offsets and connectivity, ghost marks and global ids, wherever
    their values are one contiguous block of the type Tack keeps them in, and
    a polygonal dataset's cells where it holds one kind (verts, lines or
    polygons). Ids then keep VTK's width (``id_dtype`` follows it unless
    given), and floating-point arrays are shared at their own precision with
    ``dtype=None``. The shared arrays are read-only to Tack and hold VTK's
    arrays alive; what VTK changes in them afterwards, Tack sees. What cannot
    be shared -- an origin to subtract, a type to convert, triangle strips,
    collapsed hexahedra, polyhedra -- is copied as before.

    With Metal the default device, ``copy=False`` gives Metal arrays instead, as
    Apple silicon's unified memory allows with any VTK: the buffers a Metal
    dataset handed VTK (``dataset_to_vtk(copy=False)``) come back as themselves,
    memory on whole pages is wrapped in place, and anything else is copied to
    Metal, so the dataset is on Metal throughout."""
    from tack.runtime.dispatch import get_backend

    if dtype is _DEFAULT_FLOAT:
        dtype = tack.get_default_float()
    if dtype is None and not get_backend().supports_f64:
        dtype = tack.f32
    if origin is None and dtype == tack.f32:
        origin = _far_origin(grid)
    out = _vtk_to_dataset(grid, dtype=dtype, polyhedral=polyhedral, orient=orient,
                          id_dtype=id_dtype, origin=origin, copy=copy)
    if grid.GetInformation().Has(_time_key()):
        _stamp(out, grid.GetInformation().Get(_time_key()))
    return out

dataset_to_vtk(
    data, copy=True, higher_order=False, cell_grid=False
)

Copy a tack.dataset.DataSet into a new VTK dataset; an AMRDataSet of images and rectilinear grids, its ratios the same along every axis, into a vtkOverlappingAMR (its marks as vtkGhostType arrays), any other into a vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection of a partitioned dataset per level ("level<l>"), VTK's AMR holding no curvilinear grids; a PartitionedDataSet into a vtkPartitionedDataSet of its pieces, and a dict of names to PartitionedDataSets into a vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection whose partitioned datasets carry their names (vtkCompositeDataSet.NAME()).

A structured topology over uniform coordinates gives a vtkImageData (with the direction matrix), over rectilinear ones a vtkRectilinearGrid, over explicit ones (a warped or transformed grid) a vtkStructuredGrid; an unstructured one a vtkUnstructuredGrid, a polygonal or polyline one a vtkUnstructuredGrid of VTK_POLYGON or VTK_POLY_LINE cells, and a polyhedral one a vtkUnstructuredGrid of VTK_POLYHEDRON cells, each keeping its own copy of its faces, outward for it (VTK's layout has no orientation bit, so a shared face cannot be stored once). H1 fields and values on points become point data -- an order-2 field its values at the points, the grid being linear -- and Constant fields and values on cells cell data. L2 fields have no VTK array to go to without duplicating points, and fields on faces or edges none at all; they are left out. The geometry (data.geometry) becomes the points, so it must be H1. Implicit types, offsets and connectivity, and constant and counting field values, become VTK's constant and affine arrays. Ghost marks become vtkGhostType arrays.

The step's time (data.time) becomes VTK's DATA_TIME_STEP; VTK has no unit for it.

Normals become VTK's active normals, which its renderers and filters read and a plain array is not: a 3-vector point field named Normals (VTK's readers' and filters' name) or normals (surface_normals' and point_normals'), and a 3-vector cell field named Normals, Normals (cells) or cell_normals. Tack keeps no roles of its own.

With copy=False the VTK dataset shares Tack's memory where the arrays are stored on the CPU: the points (with no origin), the field values, the cell types, offsets and connectivity (ids of one width, as VTK keeps 32-bit ids too), ghost marks and global ids. The VTK arrays hold Tack's, and writes on either side reach the other. Implicit arrays go across as VTK's implicit ones either way; anything else -- arrays on a GPU, a polyhedral topology's faces -- is copied as before. Metal arrays are shared too, with any VTK: on Apple silicon their buffers are host memory, so VTK holds views of them, after one wait for the device (MetalBuffer.share); launches that use a shared buffer complete before returning, so VTK reads what Tack wrote, and the buffers come back as themselves through vtk_to_dataset.

With higher_order, a dataset of segments, quads or hexahedra (pixels and voxels too), or of triangles, tetrahedra or wedges, whose geometry or an H1 field is above order 1 becomes VTK Lagrange cells (VTK_LAGRANGE_CURVE, _QUADRILATERAL, _HEXAHEDRON, _TRIANGLE, _TETRAHEDRON, _WEDGE) of the largest order: points at the equispaced nodes of H1 of that order, each shared node once, the geometry and H1 fields evaluated there (exact for fields of that order or below), cell fields as cell data. vtk_to_dataset reads such a grid back into those spaces. higher_order="bezier" writes VTK Bezier cells (VTK_BEZIER_CURVE, _QUADRILATERAL, _HEXAHEDRON, _TRIANGLE, _TETRAHEDRON, _WEDGE) instead: points and point data the coefficients of H1(order, basis="bernstein"), which vtk_to_dataset reads back as such; True chooses Bezier cells when the geometry or an H1 field is in a Bernstein basis, "lagrange" Lagrange cells always. higher_order="quadratic" writes VTK's classic quadratic cells (order 2): VTK_QUADRATIC_QUAD, _HEXAHEDRON and _WEDGE from serendipity (quad8, hex20, wedge15), VTK_QUADRATIC_TRIANGLE and _TETRA from the full order-2 space; True chooses them when a field is serendipity. vtk_to_dataset reads such cells into those spaces, the geometry too.

With cell_grid, the dataset becomes a vtkCellGrid (VTK's discontinuous-Galerkin cells) instead: each shape's cells a DG cell type, the geometry its shape attribute and each field an attribute, order 1 in VTK's complete basis C (shared through the points for H1, per cell for L2), higher orders in its arbitrary-order basis A (equispaced, lexicographic, as Tack's equispaced nodes; others converted there exactly), Constant fields and values on cells constant; fields of other spaces are left out with a warning. The cells come type by type, in Tack's order within each. It needs vtkDGCell.SetCellSpec, newer than VTK 9.7.1.

def dataset_to_vtk(data, copy=True, higher_order=False, cell_grid=False):
    """Copy a ``tack.dataset.DataSet`` into a new VTK dataset; an ``AMRDataSet`` of
    images and rectilinear grids, its ratios the same along every axis, into a
    ``vtkOverlappingAMR`` (its marks as ``vtkGhostType`` arrays), any other into
    a ``vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection`` of a partitioned dataset per level
    (``"level<l>"``), VTK's AMR holding no curvilinear grids; a
    ``PartitionedDataSet`` into a ``vtkPartitionedDataSet`` of its pieces, and a
    ``dict`` of names to
    ``PartitionedDataSet``s into a ``vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection`` whose
    partitioned datasets carry their names (``vtkCompositeDataSet.NAME()``).

    A structured topology over uniform coordinates gives a ``vtkImageData`` (with
    the direction matrix), over rectilinear ones a ``vtkRectilinearGrid``, over
    explicit ones (a warped or transformed grid) a ``vtkStructuredGrid``; an
    unstructured one a ``vtkUnstructuredGrid``, a polygonal or polyline one a
    ``vtkUnstructuredGrid`` of ``VTK_POLYGON`` or ``VTK_POLY_LINE`` cells, and a
    polyhedral one a ``vtkUnstructuredGrid`` of ``VTK_POLYHEDRON`` cells, each
    keeping its own copy of its faces, outward for it (VTK's layout has no
    orientation bit, so a shared face cannot be stored once).
    ``H1`` fields and values on points become point data -- an order-2 field
    its values at the points, the grid being linear -- and ``Constant`` fields
    and values on cells cell data. ``L2`` fields have no VTK array to go
    to without duplicating points, and fields on faces or edges none at
    all; they are left out. The geometry (``data.geometry``) becomes the
    points, so it must be ``H1``. Implicit types, offsets and connectivity,
    and constant and counting field values, become VTK's constant and affine
    arrays. Ghost marks become ``vtkGhostType`` arrays.

    The step's time (``data.time``) becomes VTK's ``DATA_TIME_STEP``; VTK has
    no unit for it.

    Normals become VTK's active normals, which its renderers and filters read
    and a plain array is not: a 3-vector point field named ``Normals`` (VTK's
    readers' and filters' name) or ``normals`` (``surface_normals``' and
    ``point_normals``'), and a 3-vector cell field named ``Normals``,
    ``Normals (cells)`` or ``cell_normals``. Tack keeps no roles of its own.

    With ``copy=False`` the VTK dataset shares Tack's memory where the arrays
    are stored on the CPU: the points (with no origin), the field values, the
    cell types, offsets and connectivity (ids of one width, as VTK keeps 32-bit
    ids too), ghost marks and global ids. The VTK arrays hold Tack's, and
    writes on either side reach the other. Implicit arrays go across as VTK's
    implicit ones either way; anything else -- arrays on a GPU, a polyhedral
    topology's faces -- is copied as before. Metal arrays are shared too, with
    any VTK: on Apple silicon their buffers are host memory, so VTK holds views
    of them, after one wait for the device (``MetalBuffer.share``); launches
    that use a shared buffer complete before returning, so VTK reads what Tack
    wrote, and the buffers come back as themselves through ``vtk_to_dataset``.

    With ``higher_order``, a dataset of segments, quads or hexahedra (pixels and
    voxels too), or of triangles, tetrahedra or wedges, whose geometry or an ``H1``
    field is above order 1 becomes VTK Lagrange cells (``VTK_LAGRANGE_CURVE``,
    ``_QUADRILATERAL``, ``_HEXAHEDRON``, ``_TRIANGLE``, ``_TETRAHEDRON``,
    ``_WEDGE``) of the largest order: points at the equispaced nodes of
    ``H1`` of that order, each shared node once, the geometry and ``H1`` fields
    evaluated there (exact for fields of that order or below), cell fields as
    cell data. ``vtk_to_dataset`` reads such a grid back into those spaces.
    ``higher_order="bezier"`` writes VTK Bezier cells (``VTK_BEZIER_CURVE``,
    ``_QUADRILATERAL``, ``_HEXAHEDRON``, ``_TRIANGLE``, ``_TETRAHEDRON``,
    ``_WEDGE``) instead: points and point data the
    coefficients of ``H1(order, basis="bernstein")``, which ``vtk_to_dataset``
    reads back as such; ``True`` chooses Bezier cells when the geometry or an
    ``H1`` field is in a Bernstein basis, ``"lagrange"`` Lagrange cells always.
    ``higher_order="quadratic"`` writes VTK's classic quadratic cells (order 2):
    ``VTK_QUADRATIC_QUAD``, ``_HEXAHEDRON`` and ``_WEDGE`` from serendipity (quad8,
    hex20, wedge15), ``VTK_QUADRATIC_TRIANGLE`` and ``_TETRA`` from the full order-2
    space; ``True`` chooses them when a field is serendipity. ``vtk_to_dataset``
    reads such cells into those spaces, the geometry too.

    With ``cell_grid``, the dataset becomes a ``vtkCellGrid`` (VTK's
    discontinuous-Galerkin cells) instead: each shape's cells a DG cell type, the
    geometry its shape attribute and each field an attribute, order 1 in VTK's
    complete basis ``C`` (shared through the points for ``H1``, per cell for
    ``L2``), higher orders in its arbitrary-order basis ``A`` (equispaced,
    lexicographic, as Tack's equispaced nodes; others converted there exactly),
    ``Constant`` fields and values on cells ``constant``; fields of other spaces
    are left out with a warning. The cells come type by type, in Tack's order
    within each. It needs ``vtkDGCell.SetCellSpec``, newer than VTK 9.7.1."""
    from tack.interop.vtk import _lagrange

    if cell_grid:
        from tack.interop.vtk import _cellgrid

        return _cellgrid.to_cell_grid(data)

    if higher_order not in (False, True, "lagrange", "bezier", "quadratic"):
        raise ValueError(f"higher_order is False, True, \"lagrange\", \"bezier\" or "
                         f"\"quadratic\", not {higher_order!r}")
    order = _lagrange.tensor_order(data) if higher_order else 1
    bezier = higher_order == "bezier" or (higher_order is True and _lagrange.bernstein(data))
    quadratic = higher_order == "quadratic" or (higher_order is True and order == 2
                                                and _lagrange.serendipity(data))
    if quadratic and order != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"VTK's quadratic cells are of order 2; this dataset's highest "
                         f"order is {order}")
    out = (_lagrange.to_vtk(data, order, bezier, quadratic) if order > 1
           else _dataset_to_vtk(data, copy))
    time = _time_of(data)
    if time is not None:
        from vtkmodules.vtkCommonDataModel import vtkDataObject

        out.GetInformation().Set(vtkDataObject.DATA_TIME_STEP(), time)
    return out

docs.title: tack.interop.vtk.algorithms
docs.text:
Tack's filters as VTK algorithms: VTKPythonAlgorithmBase subclasses that sit in a VTK pipeline beside VTK's own.

from vtkmodules.vtkIOXML import vtkXMLUnstructuredGridReader
from tack.interop.vtk.algorithms import Contour

reader = vtkXMLUnstructuredGridReader(file_name="mesh.vtu")
surface = (reader >> Contour(field="pressure", value=0.5))()

Each takes a vtkDataSet or a vtkPartitionedDataSet. Its input becomes a Tack dataset sharing VTK's memory (vtk_to_dataset(..., copy=False)), the filter runs on the CPU, and its result goes back to VTK sharing Tack's (dataset_to_vtk(..., copy=False)): no array is copied either way where its values are stored as Tack keeps them. A partitioned input runs the filter on each piece and gives a vtkPartitionedDataSet; the filters whose answer needs every piece (GhostCells, GenerateGlobalIds, MergePieces) take them together.

Filters that make a dataset give a vtkUnstructuredGrid (or keep a structured grid's type where the Tack filter does); filters that compute a field (Gradients, Elevation, CellQuality) give their input's type, shallow-copied, with the new arrays added.

Parameters are properties, given to the constructor or set later; setting one marks the algorithm modified. Field names are given by name (field=).

An exception in a filter is VTK's error: printed, the output left empty and Update() false. It is also kept as the algorithm's error (None after a run that succeeded), for Python callers.

def execute(self, data):

docs.title: tack.interop.mfem
docs.text:
MFEM meshes and grid functions as tack.dataset datasets, through PyMFEM.

mfem_to_dataset(mesh, fields) copies an mfem.ser.Mesh and named GridFunctions on it. The mesh's elements are the topology, and its element attributes an i32 Constant field, "attribute".

MFEM lists every element's corners in VTK's order, the prism included: both put the triangle (0, 1, 2) with its normal toward (3, 4, 5), and a positively oriented MFEM prism has a positive Jacobian as a VTK wedge, as VTK's own wedges do. (MFEM's VTK writer swaps a prism's corners 1 and 2, and 4 and 5 -- PrismMap in mesh/vtk.cpp -- which turns such a prism inside out against VTK's documented and implemented convention.)

Each grid function becomes a field in the space its collection matches:

  • H1 order 1 (H1_*_P1): an H1 field, one value per vertex, which is how MFEM numbers an order-1 H1 space's DOFs;
  • L2 order 0: a Constant field;
  • L2 order 1: an L2 field of each element's values at its corners, where MFEM evaluates its own basis (its DOFs sit at interior Gauss points, not corners). On tetrahedra, hexahedra and prisms the two spaces are the same, so this is exact; on pyramids MFEM's order-1 L2 space is not the collapsed trilinear one, and the corners interpolate it;

  • H1 order 2: an H1 order-2 field, MFEM's function evaluated at each element's quadratic nodes (corners, edge middles, quad-face middles, a hexahedron's center). MFEM's order-2 nodes are these same points, so it is exact; pyramids, whose MFEM basis is another, are refused.

  • H1 from order 3 and L2 from order 2, on quads and hexahedra: Tack's space of that order (tack.dataset.bases). On bases Tack has -- MFEM's default Gauss-Lobatto for H1 and Gauss-Legendre for L2, Gauss-Lobatto, closed uniform and positive (Bernstein, H1Pos, from order 2) for either -- the values are copied, permuted into Tack's numbering: both number a cell's nodes (a Bernstein basis' control points) lexicographically on the same reference cell, and a shared node is every element's, which is checked. On any other basis (open uniform) the function is evaluated at Tack's Gauss-Lobatto nodes, the same polynomials, so exactly.

  • The same on triangles, tetrahedra and wedges, whose Tack nodes are equispaced: MFEM's closed uniform values and positive coefficients are copied (matched by reference coordinates), and any other basis -- MFEM's default Gauss-Lobatto-based simplex nodes for H1, Gauss-Legendre for L2 -- is evaluated at Tack's equispaced lattice.

A curved mesh gets a geometry of its nodes' order the same way. Vector grid functions (vdim > 1) become fields of vectors, in either ordering. mfem_grid_function gives a field back as an MFEM GridFunction. PyMFEM (pip install mfem) is imported on first use.

The values are copied, permuted into MFEM's numbering. Keep the returned function's fes and fec attributes alive as long as it is used.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/interop/mfem.py 
def mfem_grid_function(data, field, mesh, fes=None):
    """``field``, an ``H1`` or ``L2`` field of ``data`` on quads or hexahedra (the dataset
    ``mfem_to_dataset`` made from ``mesh``), as an MFEM ``GridFunction``: on
    ``fes`` if given (its collection's nodes must be the field's), else on a new
    space of the field's family, order and nodes (``H1_FECollection`` or
    ``L2_FECollection`` with the matching basis type, MFEM's positive one for a
    Bernstein field), ``byVDIM`` for vectors.
    The values are copied, permuted into MFEM's numbering. Keep the returned
    function's ``fes`` and ``fec`` attributes alive as long as it is used."""
    from tack import arrays
    from tack.dataset import H1, L2, bases

    m = _mfem()
    space = field.space
    if not isinstance(space, (H1, L2)) or space.varies:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"an MFEM grid function of {space!r} is not supported")
    simplex = _check_tensor(data, "mfem_grid_function")
    order = space.order
    family = space.basis or ("equispaced" if simplex else "gauss_lobatto")
    if isinstance(space, L2) and order <= 1 and not space.tensor:
        raise NotImplementedError("L2 of corner values (order 0 and 1) has no MFEM basis "
                                  "of its own: project it into L2 on Gauss-Legendre nodes")
    dim = data.topology.dimension
    values = arrays.materialize(field.values).numpy().reshape(space.size, -1)
    vdim = values.shape[1]
    fec = None
    if fes is None:
        kind = {"gauss_lobatto": m.BasisType.GaussLobatto,
                "equispaced": m.BasisType.ClosedUniform,
                "gauss_legendre": m.BasisType.GaussLegendre,
                "bernstein": m.BasisType.Positive}[family]
        fec = (m.H1_FECollection if isinstance(space, H1) else m.L2_FECollection)(
            order, dim, kind)
        fes = m.FiniteElementSpace(mesh, fec, vdim, m.Ordering.byVDIM)
    if _nodes_of(fes) != family:
        raise ValueError(f"the MFEM space's nodes are not the field's ({family})")
    n = data.num_cells

    per_cell = _per_cell(data, order) if simplex else (order + 1) ** dim
    if isinstance(space, H1):
        indices = _h1_indices(data, space, per_cell).reshape(-1)
    else:
        indices = space.indices().reshape(-1)            # either layout
    mfem_dofs = _element_dofs(fes, bases.nodes(family, order), order).reshape(-1)
    by_dof = np.zeros((fes.GetNDofs(), vdim))
    by_dof[mfem_dofs] = values[indices]
    gf = m.GridFunction(fes)
    flat = by_dof.T.reshape(-1) if fes.GetOrdering() == 0 else by_dof.reshape(-1)
    gf.Assign(m.Vector(flat.astype(float)))
    gf.fes, gf.fec = fes, fec
    return gf

def mfem_field(data, mesh, gf, dtype=None, dofs=None):
    """``gf``, an MFEM grid function on ``mesh``, as a field of ``data`` (the dataset
    ``mfem_to_dataset`` made from ``mesh``). ``dofs="table"`` keeps an ``H1`` field
    of order 2 and up numbered as MFEM numbers it: its values as they are, in a
    space numbered by MFEM's element-to-DOF table (``H1(..., dofs=table)``), on the
    bases whose values are copied; by default they are permuted into Tack's
    numbering by entity."""
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    from tack.dataset import H1, L2, Constant, Field

    if dofs not in (None, "table"):
        raise ValueError(f"dofs is None or 'table', not {dofs!r}")
    fes = gf.FESpace()
    family, order = _collection(fes)
    if dofs == "table" and family == "H1" and order >= 2:
        space, values = _table_values(data, gf, order)
        return Field(space, _field_values(values, dtype))
    if family == "H1" and order == 1:
        if fes.GetNDofs() != mesh.GetNV():
            raise ValueError("an order-1 H1 space has a DOF per vertex")
        return Field(H1(data), _field_values(_by_dof(fes, gf.GetDataArray()), dtype))
    if family == "L2" and order == 0:
        return Field(Constant(data), _field_values(_by_dof(fes, gf.GetDataArray()), dtype))
    if family == "L2" and order == 1:
        return Field(L2(data), _field_values(_corner_values(mesh, gf), dtype))
    if family == "H1" and order == 2 and _nodes_of(fes) not in (None, "bernstein"):
        space, values = _quadratic_values(data, mesh, gf)
        return Field(space, _field_values(values, dtype))
    if order >= 2:
        space, values = _tensor_values(data, mesh, gf, family, order)
        return Field(space, _field_values(values, dtype))
    raise NotImplementedError(f"MFEM {family} order {order} has no space here yet")

mfem_to_dataset(

A tack.dataset.DataSet of an MFEM mesh and named grid functions on it.

The geometry is the vertex positions (z = 0 for a 2D mesh), or for a curved mesh an H1 field of positions of its nodes' order. Element attributes become fields["attribute"]. id_dtype is the topology's (tack.dataset.ids). dofs="table" numbers a curved geometry and the H1 fields of order 2 and up as MFEM does (mfem_field).

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/interop/mfem.py 
def mfem_to_dataset(mesh, fields=None, dtype=None, id_dtype=None, dofs=None):
    """A ``tack.dataset.DataSet`` of an MFEM mesh and named grid functions on it.

    The geometry is the vertex positions (z = 0 for a 2D mesh), or for a curved
    mesh an ``H1`` field of positions of its nodes' order. Element attributes
    become ``fields["attribute"]``. ``id_dtype`` is the topology's
    (``tack.dataset.ids``). ``dofs="table"`` numbers a curved geometry and the
    ``H1`` fields of order 2 and up as MFEM does (``mfem_field``).
    """
    dtype = tack.get_default_float() if dtype is None else dtype
    from tack.dataset import L2, Constant, DataSet, Field

    if dofs not in (None, "table"):
        raise ValueError(f"dofs is None or 'table', not {dofs!r}")
    nodes = mesh.GetNodes()
    # A periodic mesh keeps its nodes per element (L2), so the two sides of a
    # periodic seam can differ: an L2 geometry, on the identified vertices.
    periodic = nodes is not None and _collection(nodes.FESpace())[0] == "L2"
    curved = nodes is not None and not periodic and _collection(nodes.FESpace())[1] > 1
    order = _collection(nodes.FESpace())[1] if curved or periodic else 1
    topology = _topology(mesh, id_dtype)
    if curved or periodic:
        positions = np.asarray(mesh.GetVertexArray(), dtype=float).reshape(
            mesh.GetNV(), mesh.SpaceDimension())
    elif nodes is not None:
        # Order-1 nodes are the vertices' positions, and may have moved since
        # the vertex array was set (Mesh.Transform moves the nodes).
        positions = _by_dof(nodes.FESpace(), nodes.GetDataArray())
    else:
        positions = np.asarray(mesh.GetVertexArray(), dtype=float).reshape(
            mesh.GetNV(), mesh.SpaceDimension())
    if positions.shape[1] < 3:
        positions = np.hstack([positions, np.zeros((positions.shape[0],
                                                    3 - positions.shape[1]))])
    data = DataSet(topology, positions, dtype=dtype)
    if curved:
        # The corners first, to have a dataset to number the nodes on; then the
        # curved geometry, MFEM's nodes at those nodes.
        if dofs == "table":
            space, values = _table_values(data, nodes, order)
        elif order == 2 and _nodes_of(nodes.FESpace()) not in (None, "bernstein"):
            space, values = _quadratic_values(data, mesh, nodes)
        else:
            space, values = _tensor_values(data, mesh, nodes, "H1", order)
        if values.shape[1] < 3:
            # A 2D mesh's nodes have two components; positions are three.
            values = np.hstack([values, np.zeros((values.shape[0], 3 - values.shape[1]))])
        data.geometry = Field(space, _field_values(values, dtype))
    elif periodic:
        if order == 1:
            space, values = L2(data), _corner_values(mesh, nodes)
        else:
            space, values = _tensor_values(data, mesh, nodes, "L2", order)
        if values.shape[1] < 3:
            values = np.hstack([values, np.zeros((values.shape[0], 3 - values.shape[1]))])
        data.geometry = Field(space, _field_values(values, dtype))
    attributes = np.array([mesh.GetAttribute(e) for e in range(mesh.GetNE())], np.int32)
    data.fields["attribute"] = Field(Constant(data), _field_values(attributes, tack.i32))
    for name, gf in (fields or {}).items():
        data.fields[name] = mfem_field(data, mesh, gf, dtype=dtype, dofs=dofs)
    return data

docs.title: tack.interop.warp
docs.text:
Arrays and datasets between Tack and NVIDIA Warp, without copies where they agree.

With the Warp device (tack.device("warp")) a Tack array's memory is a wp.array on Warp's device, and Tack launches on that device's current Warp stream, the stream a caller's wp.launch uses. So a program can run its own Warp kernels and Tack's filters on the same arrays:

tack.set_default_device("warp")
wp.launch(my_kernel, n, inputs=[f])
data.fields["f"] = td.Field(td.H1(data), from_warp(f))
iso = alg.contour(data, "f", 0.5)
points = to_warp(iso.geometry.values)          # a wp.array of wp.vec3

from_warp and to_warp map Warp's vector and matrix types to Tack's (wp.vec3 and tack.vec(3, tack.f32), wp.mat33 and tack.mat(3, 3, tack.f32)), keep the other side's memory alive for as long as the result lives, and do not mark the memory as handed outside Tack: on one device and stream, Tack's launches need not complete before returning. Under wp.ScopedStream Tack follows the scope's stream too.

Warp arrays have no read-only flag: a read-only Tack array given to Warp can be written there.

to_simdata and from_simdata exchange datasets with warp-simdata (NVIDIA's simulation-data library on Warp, an optional import): image data, structured grids, polydata and unstructured grids (polyhedra included) against Tack's topologies, NODE and ELEMENT fields against point and cell fields, collections against partitioned datasets. Most of warp-simdata's other models come across as they are, sharing their arrays (see from_simdata); the rest through its to_vtk_data_model.

The element type follows Warp's (wp.vec3 gives tack.vec(3, tack.f32)) and the shape is the array's. The Tack array keeps array alive. array must be on the device Tack's Warp device drives (Warp's default device).

def from_warp(array, *, writable=True):
    """``array``, a contiguous ``wp.array``, as a Tack array on the Warp device,
    sharing its memory: a write through either is seen by the other.

    The element type follows Warp's (``wp.vec3`` gives ``tack.vec(3,
    tack.f32)``) and the shape is the array's. The Tack array keeps
    ``array`` alive. ``array`` must be on the device Tack's Warp device
    drives (Warp's default device).
    """
    from tack.runtime.warp_backend import WarpBuffer
    wp = _warp()
    if not isinstance(array, wp.array):
        raise TypeError(f"from_warp takes a wp.array, not {type(array).__name__}")
    if not array.is_contiguous:
        raise ValueError("from_warp wraps a contiguous wp.array; copy it with "
                         "wp.clone first")
    backend = _warp_backend()
    if str(array.device) != str(backend.wp_device):
        raise ValueError(f"the array is on Warp's {array.device}, but Tack's Warp device "
                         f"drives {backend.wp_device} (Warp's default device)")
    dtype = _tack_dtype(array.dtype)
    shape = tuple(array.shape)
    scalar = dtype.scalar_dtype if isinstance(dtype, ElementType) else dtype
    count = math.prod(shape) * (dtype.size if isinstance(dtype, ElementType) else 1)
    storage = (count,) if isinstance(dtype, ElementType) else shape
    if count:
        flat = wp.array(ptr=array.ptr, dtype=_warp_dtype(scalar), shape=(count,),
                        capacity=count * np.dtype(scalar.numpy_dtype).itemsize,
                        device=array.device)
    else:
        flat = None                     # nothing to share; WarpBuffer makes its own
    buffer = WarpBuffer(backend, scalar, storage, flat)
    buffer._owner = array               # the memory lives as long as the Tack array
    return _array_view(dtype, shape, buffer, writable=writable, device=backend)

docs.text:
to_warp(array)

array as a wp.array sharing its memory, with Warp's element type (tack.vec(3, tack.f32) gives wp.vec3) at its logical shape.

An array on the Warp device is its own memory, kept alive by the result. An array on another Tack device goes through DLPack, which completes its queued launches. An implicit array (tack.arrays: ConstantArray, UniformCoordinates, ...) has no memory, and is materialized on its device first. Structure-of-arrays storage has no single wp.array; give its components one at a time.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/interop/warp.py 
def to_warp(array):
    """``array`` as a ``wp.array`` sharing its memory, with Warp's element type
    (``tack.vec(3, tack.f32)`` gives ``wp.vec3``) at its logical shape.

    An array on the Warp device is its own memory, kept alive by the result.
    An array on another Tack device goes through DLPack, which completes its
    queued launches. An implicit array (``tack.arrays``: ``ConstantArray``,
    ``UniformCoordinates``, ...) has no memory, and is materialized on its
    device first. Structure-of-arrays storage has no single ``wp.array``;
    give its components one at a time.
    """
    wp = _warp()
    if isinstance(array, _Implicit):
        array = materialize(array)
    if isinstance(array, SoaArray):
        raise TypeError("a structure-of-arrays array has no single wp.array; "
                        "give its components (array.components) one at a time")
    if not isinstance(array, Array):
        raise TypeError(f"to_warp takes a Tack array, not {type(array).__name__}")
    shape, dtype, nbytes = tuple(array.shape), array.dtype, array._buffer.nbytes
    backend = array._device
    if backend.name == "warp":
        address, device = array._buffer.address, backend.wp_device
    else:
        source = wp.from_dlpack(array)          # Tack's export completes its launches
        address, device = source.ptr, source.device
        array = (array, source)                 # keep both alive
    if not math.prod(shape):
        return wp.empty(shape, dtype=_warp_dtype(dtype), device=device)

    def keep(_ptr, _size, _held=array):
        """Warp calls this when the result is freed; it holds the Tack array till then."""

    return wp.array(ptr=address, dtype=_warp_dtype(dtype), shape=shape, capacity=nbytes,
                    device=device, deleter=keep)

docs.text:
to_simdata(data)

A Tack DataSet (or PartitionedDataSet) as a warp-simdata dataset (or DatasetCollection) on Warp's device.

A uniform grid becomes image data (an origin, a spacing and an extent; a rotated one becomes a structured grid), any other structured grid a structured grid, polygons and polylines polydata, and every other topology an unstructured grid, polyhedra with their faces. Point fields become NODE fields and cell fields ELEMENT ones. Arrays already f32 positions, i32 ids and u8 types on the Warp device are shared; others are copied, positions as f32 world positions (Tack's origin added, so far coordinates lose the precision the origin kept). Ghost marks, global ids, sets, units and time have no counterpart there and are left behind.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/interop/warp.py 
def to_simdata(data):
    """A Tack ``DataSet`` (or ``PartitionedDataSet``) as a warp-simdata dataset (or
    ``DatasetCollection``) on Warp's device.

    A uniform grid becomes image data (an origin, a spacing and an extent; a
    rotated one becomes a structured grid), any other structured grid a
    structured grid, polygons and polylines polydata, and every other topology
    an unstructured grid, polyhedra with their faces. Point fields become NODE
    fields and cell fields ELEMENT ones. Arrays already f32 positions, i32 ids
    and u8 types on the Warp device are shared; others are copied, positions
    as f32 world positions (Tack's origin added, so far coordinates lose the
    precision the origin kept). Ghost marks, global ids, sets, units and time
    have no counterpart there and are left behind.
    """
    sd = _simdata()
    from warp_simdata.data_models.vtk import (
        image_data,
        polydata,
        structured_grid,
        unstructured_grid,
    )

    from tack.arrays import UniformCoordinates
    from tack.dataset import (
        PartitionedDataSet,
        PolygonalTopology,
        PolyhedralTopology,
        PolylineTopology,
        StructuredTopology,
    )

    wp = _warp()
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from warp_simdata.data_models.vtk.conversion import to_common_vtk_data_model
        return sd.DatasetCollection.from_datasets(
            to_common_vtk_data_model([to_simdata(piece) for piece in data]))
    device = _wp_device(data)
    topology, coordinates = data.topology, data.geometry.values
    if isinstance(topology, StructuredTopology):
        dims = list(topology.point_dims) + [1] * (3 - len(topology.point_dims))
        lo = list(topology.offset) + [0] * (3 - len(topology.offset))
        hi = [o + d - 1 for o, d in zip(lo, dims)]
        if isinstance(coordinates, UniformCoordinates) and np.allclose(
                coordinates._matrix, np.eye(3)):
            spacing = np.asarray(coordinates._spacing, np.float64)
            start = np.asarray(coordinates._origin, np.float64) + np.asarray(data.origin)
            out = image_data.create_dataset(
                origin=wp.vec3f(*(start - np.asarray(lo) * spacing)),   # node ijk at 0, as VTK
                spacing=wp.vec3f(*spacing), extent_min=wp.vec3i(*lo),
                extent_max=wp.vec3i(*hi), device=str(device))
        else:
            out = structured_grid.create_dataset(_points(data, device), wp.vec3i(*lo),
                                                 wp.vec3i(*hi))
    elif isinstance(topology, (PolygonalTopology, PolylineTopology)):
        polygons = isinstance(topology, PolygonalTopology)
        offsets, points = topology.loops() if polygons else topology.lines()
        rings = {"polys_offsets" if polygons else "lines_offsets":
                 _shared_or_copied(offsets, wp.int32, device),
                 "polys_connectivity" if polygons else "lines_connectivity":
                 _shared_or_copied(points, wp.int32, device)}
        out = polydata.create_dataset(_points(data, device), **rings)
    elif isinstance(topology, PolyhedralTopology):
        # Faces shared between cells: warp-simdata finds each cell's outward
        # winding itself (its face orientations).
        point_offsets, point_ids = topology.cell_points()
        out = unstructured_grid.create_dataset(
            _points(data, device),
            wp.full(topology.num_cells, 42, dtype=wp.uint8, device=device),
            _shared_or_copied(point_offsets, wp.int32, device),
            _shared_or_copied(point_ids, wp.int32, device),
            faces_offsets=_shared_or_copied(topology.face_offsets, wp.int32, device),
            faces_connectivity=_shared_or_copied(topology.face_points, wp.int32, device),
            face_locations_offsets=_shared_or_copied(topology.cell_offsets, wp.int32, device),
            face_locations_connectivity=_shared_or_copied(topology.cell_faces, wp.int32,
                                                          device))
    else:
        out = unstructured_grid.create_dataset(
            _points(data, device),
            _shared_or_copied(topology.types, wp.uint8, device),
            _shared_or_copied(topology.offsets, wp.int32, device),
            _shared_or_copied(topology.connectivity, wp.int32, device))
    _add_fields(data, out, device)
    return out

docs.title: from_simdata
docs.text:
from_simdata(ds)

A warp-simdata dataset (or DatasetCollection) as a Tack DataSet (or PartitionedDataSet) on the Warp device, sharing its arrays.

Point clouds, curves, surface meshes, OpenFOAM polyMesh and boundary patches, CGNS sections of linear elements (one shape, MIXED, NGON_n and NFACE_n), EnSight parts of one kind, corner-point grids (inactive cells hidden) and FLASH axisymmetric data (an AMRDataSet of revolved boxes) are taken as they are: their arrays become Tack's, CGNS's 1-based and MIXED connectivities read lazily (see "models imported as they are"). Every other model goes through warp-simdata's to_vtk_data_model first. Image data becomes a uniform grid (offset from its extent), a structured grid a structured topology over its points, polydata of polygons or polylines a polygonal or polyline topology (vertices alone become vertex cells; a mix of kinds is refused: split it first), and an unstructured grid an unstructured topology, or a polyhedral one when it has polyhedra. NODE fields become H1 fields and ELEMENT fields Constant ones. The dataset must be on the device Tack's Warp device drives.

Source code in packages/tack-vis/src/tack/interop/warp.py 
def from_simdata(ds):
    """A warp-simdata dataset (or ``DatasetCollection``) as a Tack ``DataSet`` (or
    ``PartitionedDataSet``) on the Warp device, sharing its arrays.

    Point clouds, curves, surface meshes, OpenFOAM polyMesh and boundary
    patches, CGNS sections of linear elements (one shape, MIXED, NGON_n and
    NFACE_n), EnSight parts of one kind, corner-point grids (inactive cells
    hidden) and FLASH axisymmetric data (an ``AMRDataSet`` of revolved boxes)
    are taken as they are: their arrays become Tack's, CGNS's 1-based and MIXED
    connectivities read lazily (see "models imported as they are"). Every
    other model goes through warp-simdata's ``to_vtk_data_model`` first. Image data becomes a uniform grid (``offset`` from its extent), a structured
    grid a structured topology over its points, polydata of polygons or
    polylines a polygonal or polyline topology (vertices alone become vertex
    cells; a mix of kinds is refused: split it first), and an unstructured grid
    an unstructured topology, or a polyhedral one when it has polyhedra. NODE
    fields become H1 fields and ELEMENT fields Constant ones. The dataset must
    be on the device Tack's Warp device drives.
    """
    sd = _simdata()
    from warp_simdata.data_models.vtk import (
        image_data,
        polydata,
        structured_grid,
        unstructured_grid,
    )
    from warp_simdata.data_models.vtk.conversion import to_vtk_data_model

    from tack.arrays import ConstantArray, UniformCoordinates
    from tack.dataset import (
        PartitionedDataSet,
        PolygonalTopology,
        PolyhedralTopology,
        PolylineTopology,
        UnstructuredTopology,
    )
    from tack.dataset.dataset import grid_topology

    if isinstance(ds, sd.DatasetCollection):
        pieces = ds.datasets
        if any(not piece.has_field(name) for name in ds.get_field_names() for piece in pieces):
            # Fields of the collection itself: its VTK conversion hands them out.
            pieces = to_vtk_data_model(ds).datasets
        return PartitionedDataSet(from_simdata(piece) for piece in pieces)
    device = tack.device("warp")
    from warp_simdata.data_models.flash import axisymmetric as flash_model
    if ds.data_model is flash_model.DataModel:
        return _flash_amr(ds, device)
    with device:
        direct = _direct_topology(ds, device)
        if direct is None:
            more = _more_direct(ds, device)
            if more is not None:
                topology, geometry, ghosts = more
                return _with_fields(ds, topology, geometry, device, ghosts)
    if direct is not None:
        return _with_fields(ds, *direct, device)
    ds = to_vtk_data_model(ds)
    handle, kind = ds.handle, ds.data_model.DatasetHandle
    if kind is image_data.DatasetHandle:
        lo = np.asarray(handle.extent_min, np.int64)
        dims = np.asarray(handle.extent_max, np.int64) - lo + 1
        spacing = np.asarray(handle.spacing, np.float64)
        start = np.asarray(handle.origin, np.float64) + lo * spacing
        topology = grid_topology(dims.tolist(), offset=lo.tolist(), device=device)
        geometry = UniformCoordinates(dims.tolist(), start, spacing, np.eye(3), device=device)
    elif kind is structured_grid.DatasetHandle:
        lo = np.asarray(handle.extent_min, np.int64)
        dims = np.asarray(handle.extent_max, np.int64) - lo + 1
        topology = grid_topology(dims.tolist(), offset=lo.tolist(), device=device)
        geometry = from_warp(handle.points)
    elif kind is polydata.DatasetHandle:
        def present(offsets):
            return offsets is not None and offsets.shape[0] > 1
        kinds = [k for k in ("verts", "lines", "polys") if present(getattr(handle, f"{k}_offsets"))]
        if len(kinds) > 1:
            raise ValueError(f"polydata of {' and '.join(kinds)} together has no one Tack "
                             "topology: split it by kind first")
        n = ds.get_num_nodes()
        kind = kinds[0] if kinds else "verts"
        offsets = getattr(handle, f"{kind}_offsets")
        points = getattr(handle, f"{kind}_connectivity")
        offsets = from_warp(offsets) if present(offsets) else np.zeros(1, np.int32)
        points = from_warp(points) if present(getattr(handle, f"{kind}_offsets")) \
            else np.zeros(0, np.int32)
        with device:                        # host arrays among them go to the Warp device
            if kind == "polys":
                topology = PolygonalTopology(offsets, points, num_points=n)
            elif kind == "lines":
                topology = PolylineTopology(offsets, points, num_points=n)
            else:
                count = (len(offsets) if isinstance(offsets, np.ndarray) else offsets.shape[0]) - 1
                if points.shape[0] == count:
                    # One point each: every cell a VTK_VERTEX, an implicit array stored
                    # nowhere, as Tack's own point clouds' (uniform_cells).
                    types = ConstantArray(1, count, dtype=tack.u8)
                else:
                    # Poly-vertices among them (VTK_POLY_VERTEX, 2): a type per cell.
                    counts = np.diff(offsets.numpy() if isinstance(offsets, Array) else offsets)
                    types = np.where(counts == 1, 1, 2).astype(np.uint8)
                topology = UnstructuredTopology(types, offsets, points, num_points=n)
        geometry = from_warp(handle.points)
    elif kind is unstructured_grid.DatasetHandle:
        n = ds.get_num_nodes()
        types = from_warp(handle.cell_types)
        present = _present_types(types)
        if 42 in present:
            with device:                    # its new arrays on the Warp device
                topology = _polyhedra_from_simdata(handle, PolyhedralTopology, n)
        else:
            topology = UnstructuredTopology(types, from_warp(handle.cell_offsets),
                                            from_warp(handle.cell_connectivity), num_points=n)
        geometry = from_warp(handle.points)
    else:
        raise TypeError(f"no Tack topology for warp-simdata's {kind.__name__}")
    return _with_fields(ds, topology, geometry, device)

docs.title: Dataset API
docs.text:
tack.dataset, in the tack-vis package. This page describes the API as it stands; the Visualization Guide develops the model, mesh construction, field spaces, filters, mesh kernels and complete pipelines with checked examples. For why it is shaped this way and how it got here, see the design records: Dataset API and Polyhedra. They are history; this page is the current state. What is missing is listed with each part, and under Settled, and open. Each algorithm's and class's signature and parameters are in Algorithms and Data Model.

import tack.dataset as td
from tack.dataset import algorithms as alg

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
• A DataSet is a topology, named fields and named sets.
  • A topology is cells and the entities derived from them: faces, edges and points, and which cells lie on each side of a face.
  • A Field is a space and its values.
  • A space says where values live and how they are interpolated, if at all. It is built on a topology and owns its layout.
  • The geometry is a field, so point positions are data like any other. It is kept apart from the named fields, as data.geometry. Its values are relative to the dataset's origin, three doubles on the host (Origins and point clouds).
  • Kernels run over an iteration domain (cells, faces, edges or a face set) through for_each. That makes one launch per group of like entities, and each field argument becomes a view specialized to the group.
data = td.rectilinear_grid(np.linspace(0, 1, 11), np.linspace(0, 1, 11), [0.0, 1.0])
x = data.positions()
data.fields["height"] = td.Field(td.H1(data), scalars(x[:, 2] + 0.25 * x[:, 0]))
gradient = alg.gradients(data, data.fields["height"])     # a field on the cells

Here scalars stands for any function that puts a host array in a tack.Array.

docs.title: Import path migration
docs.text: The package is tack.dataset (previously tack.data). Change import tack.data as td to import tack.dataset as td, and use tack.dataset.<submodule> for direct imports. Existing td.DataSet, td.Field, spaces, topologies and algorithm calls keep their names and signatures. The shorthand td means Tack datasets.

docs.title: Topologies
docs.text:
There are two kinds. Shape-based topologies have cells of fixed shapes, each with a reference element: counts, tables and shape functions are compile-time constants. Polyhedral topologies have cells that are lists of faces of any size, with no reference element. They are separate paths that share everything else: spaces without a basis, fields, sets, for_each, the face conventions, and a common set of methods on cell views. topology.reference_cells says which kind a topology is.

Topology Built from Kind UnstructuredTopology(types, offsets, connectivity, num_points=None, id_dtype=None) VTK cell types and point rows, of the linear shapes (vertex to pyramid) shape-based StructuredTopology(point_dims, id_dtype=None, offset=None), usually through rectilinear_grid(x, y, z) grid dimensions; cells addressed by (i, j, k); offset, the grid index of its first point in a larger grid (VTK's extent's start: split's pieces, an image whose extent starts elsewhere) shape-based PolyhedralTopology(face_offsets, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces, cell_face_sides, num_points=None, id_dtype=None) faces stored once, as point rings wound out of side 0; each cell a list of faces, with the side (u8, 0 or 1) it is on polyhedral, 3D PolyhedralTopology.from_cell_faces(cells, num_points, positions=None, orient=False, id_dtype=None) each cell's own face rings, as VTK and most readers give them; copies of a face matched by point set polyhedral, 3D PolygonalTopology(loop_offsets, loop_points, num_points=None, id_dtype=None) each polygon's loop of points polyhedral, 2D PolylineTopology(line_offsets, line_points, num_points=None, id_dtype=None) each polyline's chain of points, two or more; a chain may close polyhedral, 1D

num_points exists because a dataset may have points that no cell uses.

Implicit topology arrays. An UnstructuredTopology's types, offsets and connectivity may each be an implicit array from tack.arrays, kept as it is and computed where it is read, as Viskores' single-type cell sets keep theirs:

  • the types of cells all of one shape, a ConstantArray (u8);
  • the offsets of cells all of one size, a CountingArray with that size as its step;
  • the connectivity of cells that each have their own points (vertex cells, a 2D contour's lines), a CountingArray too.

uniform_cells(shape_id, count, id_dtype) in tack.dataset.topology makes the first two. Filters whose output cells are all one shape give them: contour and slice (triangles, or lines in 2D), tetrahedralize, triangulate, extract_edges, the point extractions and probe's vertex cells (all three implicit), and threshold, extract_cells, extract_geometry and mask of a topology of one shape. A topology of one shape groups its cells without a histogram of their types. Everything else reads them as it reads stored ones; numpy() computes them on the host.

dataset_to_vtk hands them over as VTK's own: a ConstantArray of types becomes the cell type given as a number (VTK keeps it as a vtkConstantArray), a CountingArray a vtkAffineArray. vtk_to_dataset takes VTK's constant and affine arrays back as ConstantArray and CountingArray.

docs.title: Ids
docs.text:
Every id a topology stores or derives has one integer type, topology.id_dtype (also data.id_dtype): point and cell ids, offsets, faces, edges, point links, and the orders and keys that sort them. It is i32 unless the topology:

  • is asked for i64 (id_dtype=tack.i64);
  • is built from i64 fields;
  • or is too large for i32: an id, an offset or a derived array past 2^31 − 1 entries (a mesh's edges number up to twelve per cell).

Asked for i32, a topology too large for it raises, so a valid mesh's ids (each below num_points) are never wrapped. Arrays from NumPy or VTK (whose ids are 64-bit) take the narrowest type that holds them. Kernels specialize on their fields' types, so the same kernels serve both, and an i32 mesh pays nothing for the i64 path.

A filter's output keeps its input's type, or takes i64 when the output can be too large for i32 (a hexahedron tetrahedralizes into 24 connectivity entries), so a pipeline that starts in i64 stays there. Sort keys are tuples of ids, never ids packed into one integer, so 64-bit ids sort as 32-bit ones do.

On GPUs without 64-bit atomics (Metal, Level Zero), CellLocator's search from the cells refuses a dataset of more than 2^30 − 1 cells (it ranks a point's candidate cells up to twice the cell count in an atomic minimum); the search from the points uses no atomics, and everything else works there.

pytest --ids=i64 runs the dataset tests with every topology in i64.

docs.title: Derived entities
docs.text:
• topology.faces() and topology.edges() are derived on the device by sorting, the first time they are asked for, and then kept.
  • Faces are codimension 1 of the cells of the highest dimension (topology.dimension): a 3D mesh's faces are polygons, a 2D mesh's are its edges, on the shape path as on the polygonal one. A 2D cell's faces go round it (VTK counts none). A mesh mixing dimensions takes its faces from its top-dimensional cells alone.
  • On a 2D mesh face_geometry gives each edge's normal in the plane of its side 0's cell, pointing out of it, and its length as its "area"; face_centers its midpoint. net_flux, divergence, perot, jump and upwind_flux then work on 2D meshes as on 3D ones.
  • A mesh of line cells (a 1D grid's, or VTK lines) has no faces yet: a line's would be its end points, which are not derived, so faces() and everything built on it (face_geometry, extract_surface, side traces, jump, upwind_flux, ...) raise NotImplementedError. A polyline topology's have them.
  • A cell of no volume (a hexahedron whose points coincide, a grid of spacing 0), or a face or polygon of no area, has measure 0, its centroid at the mean of its points, and normals of zero length, so upwind_flux through it is 0. What divides by the measure has no value there: its gradients, flow_quantities and perot are NaN.
  • A polyline topology's faces are the chains' ends, one per point that chains end at: side 0 is the first chain ending there (in cell order), side 1 the second, and the normal runs along side 0's chain, out of it, with an "area" of 1. A vertex has no winding, so any two chains meeting end to end are consistent. Three or more ending at one point (a branch) have no faces: faces() refuses them, as an edge of three polygons is refused, while everything that does not need faces still works.
  • A face's points are wound out of its side 0. Side 1 is the cell on the other side, or none (-1) on the boundary.
  • Each cell knows, per local face, the face's id and which side of it the cell is on.
  • On a polyhedral topology the faces are given, not derived, and keep their given numbering.
  • A polyhedral topology also derives each cell's distinct points (cell_points()), for point data.

docs.title: Converting and checking
docs.text:
Function What it does as_polyhedra(data) a 3D shape-based dataset as polyhedra, carrying its fields as_polygons(data) a 2D shape-based dataset as polygons check_winding(data) of polyhedra or polygons, a cell Set of the cells whose faces do not wind consistently; empty when all is well (a shape's faces come from its table) orient(topology) turns around faces wound into their only cell from_cell_faces(..., orient=True) repairs input whose faces or cells are inconsistently wound, then turns each connected piece outward by the sign of its total volume topology.validate() checks the arrays a topology is built from, on their device, reading back a few integers: offsets start at 0, never run backwards and end at their members' length; every id is within its range (points; faces, for polyhedra; sides 0 or 1); an unstructured topology's types are linear shapes with their point counts. Raises ValueError saying what is wrong and how often, or returns the topology

Winding comes from the input, not from geometry. Inconsistent input is refused unless the caller asks for the repair.

A topology is not checked when made: a bad id is read, or written, out of bounds by whatever uses it first. Call validate() on input you did not make, or turn on debug mode (tack.set_debug(True), TACK_DEBUG=1), which checks every topology's ids when it is made -- before a polygonal or polyline topology derives anything from them -- along with every kernel's array accesses.

docs.title: Spaces
docs.text:
Space Values Interpolated Topologies H1(data, order=1) one per point, shared by the cells around it; order 2 adds one per edge and quad face; order p (basis=) p - 1 per edge, (p - 1)^2 per quad face, (p - 1)^d per cell yes, continuous order 1 on all; order 2 on tetrahedra, hexahedra, voxels, wedges, triangles, quads and pixels; any order on segments, quads, pixels, hexahedra and voxels, and on triangles, tetrahedra and wedges with nodes="equispaced" ((p - 1)(p - 2)/2 per triangle face, (p - 1)(p - 2)(p - 3)/6 per tetrahedron, (p - 1)^2 (p - 2)/2 per wedge) L2(data, order=1) each cell's own copies: order 1 one per corner, order 0 one per cell; order may be an array, one order per cell; a tensor basis' values in blocks or cell-fastest (layout=, by device by default) yes, discontinuous shape-based Constant(data) one per cell yes, constant in the cell all Values(data, on, oriented=False) one per point, edge, face or cell: data about the entity, with no basis no all SideTraces(data) per face, per side, per face point; made by project into it through the face's shape shape-based, 3D
  • Identity. A space is interned on its topology: H1(data) is the same object every time, so fields on it share its layout. Two spaces with different parameters are different objects.
  • Size. Every space knows its size. A field of the wrong length, or a field from another topology, is refused.
  • Continuity follows from where the values live (MFEM's model): values on shared entities are continuous, and values owned per cell are not.
  • Oriented face values. oriented=True is for a quantity measured along the face's normal, such as a normal flux. Anything that turns a face around (threshold, orient) negates such values. Plain face values (an area, an id) are left alone.

Attributes: topology, size, on (the entity kind the values are indexed by), interpolated, and order where it applies.

docs.title: Moving a field between spaces
docs.text:
project(data, field, space) gives field in another space of the same topology, as a new field. Values on points or cells count as order-1 H1 and Constant, as source and as target.

Into Each value is Exact when H1 (order 1 or 2) the mean, over the cells around the node, of the source evaluated there the source is continuous: a lower order comes across exactly Constant, order-0 L2 the mean of the cell's corner values (vtkPointDataToCellData) the source is constant in the cell order-1 L2 (or an order per cell) the source's value at each corner (the corner mean at order 0) the source's order is at most 1 SideTraces each side's value from its cell always

Where cells disagree -- cell data, DG data -- the H1 mean is VTK's averaging (vtkCellDataToPointData). Sums run in a fixed order. Scalars or vectors; floating point. Values on faces or edges have no basis and are refused. On polyhedra, polygons and polylines only cell and point values project, each into the other.

Unused points retain their values when the source is H1 (or values on points). Cell or DG sources give unused points zero, since no cell contributes there.

project is the one way to move a field: into H1(data) for point values, Constant(data) for one value per cell, L2(data) for each cell's own copies, SideTraces(data) for each side's value at the faces.

docs.title: A field from a function of position
docs.text:
interpolate(data, function, space, dtype=None) is the field in space whose values are function at the space's nodes. function is a @tack.func of a world position (a 3-vector of the geometry's type) that returns a scalar or a vector; dtype is what it returns, data.dtype by default (dtype=tack.vec3() for 3-vectors).

@tack.func
def temperature(x):
    return x.x * x.x + 2.0 * x.y

data.fields["t"] = td.interpolate(data, temperature, td.H1(data, order=2))
Space Its nodes H1 the points; at order 2 also edge middles, quad face centers and cell centers; at order p the products of the 1D nodes on each edge, quad face and cell order-1 L2 each cell's corners Constant, order-0 L2, Values(data, "cells") each cell's parametric center Values(data, "points") the points
  • Node positions come from the geometry as they are needed (a curved geometry's included) and are never stored.
  • A node shared by several cells is evaluated once, by the first cell that has it (cells in group order). Which cell writes each node is kept on the space, so a changed geometry is seen. A discontinuous (L2) geometry gives a shared node the first cell's position.
  • A point no cell uses takes function at its own position when the geometry is H1, and zero when it is L2.
  • A polynomial of the space's order on straight cells is represented exactly; anything else gets the space's nodal interpolant.
  • On polyhedra, polygons and polylines only point values (H1 of order 1, Values(data, "points")) interpolate, from an H1 geometry.

docs.title: Fields and arrays
docs.text:
Field(space, values): the values are a tack.Array with a scalar or vector element dtype, or an implicit array from tack.arrays (in tack-core). An array's shape counts coefficient values; its dtype controls components. The space supplies their mesh association and basis. The implicit arrays, all in tack.arrays, are indexable in any kernel as a stored array is (a[k], len(a)), not only through a field:

Array Value k VTK Viskores ConstantArray(value, size, dtype=None, device=None) value, a scalar or a vector vtkConstantArray ArrayHandleConstant CountingArray(size, start=0, step=1, dtype=None) start + step * k vtkAffineArray ArrayHandleCounting CartesianProduct(x, y=(0.0,), z=(0.0,), device=None) a rectilinear grid's point, from three axes vtkStructuredPointArray ArrayHandleCartesianProduct UniformCoordinates(dims, origin, spacing, direction=None) an image's point, origin + direction @ (ijk * spacing) vtkStructuredPointArray ArrayHandleUniformPointCoordinates Permutation(ids, base) base[ids[k]] vtkIndexedArray ArrayHandlePermutation Concatenate(a, b, ...) the arrays end to end vtkCompositeArray ArrayHandleConcatenate Strided(values, stride, offset=0, size=None) values[offset + stride * k] of a scalar field vtkStridedArray ArrayHandleStride View(base, start, size) base[start + k] -- ArrayHandleView ExtractComponent(base, c) component c of base[k] -- ArrayHandleExtractComponent Components(a, b, ...) two to four scalar arrays as a vector -- ArrayHandleCompositeVector Function(func, size, dtype=tack.f32, width=None) func(k), a @tack.func vtkStdFunctionArray ArrayHandleImplicit Transform(func, base, dtype=None, width=None) func(base[k]) -- ArrayHandleTransform Cast(base, dtype) base[k] converted -- ArrayHandleCast RandomUniform(size, seed, low, high), RandomNormal(size, seed, mean, stddev) draws from tack.random, a pure function of k and seed -- ArrayHandleRandomUniformReal, ...StandardNormal

An array's operands are any arrays -- implicit, or device fields -- so they compose to any depth: Permutation(ids, Concatenate(field, CountingArray(...))) is an array. Every algorithm takes one unchanged: a field's view holds it as a nested template (tack.device_class objects may hold others) and reads array.get(k), which inlines to the expression one would write by hand. A composed array therefore costs nothing per value beyond what it computes; each level of nesting costs about 8 us per kernel launch on the host. VTK's vtkStdFunctionArray runs a C++ function on the CPU; a Function or Transform is a @tack.func, so it runs in the kernel on every backend. materialize(array) stores one, by a kernel; to_host reads one back. A NumPy array is refused as values: copy it with tack.array(host, dtype=...) first.

uniform_grid(dims, origin, spacing, direction=None) is a dataset on UniformCoordinates, as rectilinear_grid(x, y, z) is on a CartesianProduct; sources.wavelet and sources.tangle are uniform grids. The VTK interop reads and writes vtkImageData as uniform grids, direction matrix included. A size of 1 adds no cells, in any position: (1, 3) is a line of three points along y, as (3, 1) is along x. A grid with no axis of two or more points has no cells: (1, 1, 1) is one point, and a size of 0 makes it empty. Their topology is then an UnstructuredTopology without cells, and the VTK interop still writes them as vtkImageData (or vtkRectilinearGrid).

Geometry. DataSet(topology, geometry, fields=None, sets=None, dtype=tack.f32) takes the geometry as an H1 or L2 field of 3-vectors, or as positions per point (any array of 3-vectors), which become an H1 field. It is kept apart from fields: data.geometry returns it, assigning data.geometry replaces it (checked as the constructor checks it), and data.positions() gives the positions on the host. Algorithms move it with the cells; it is never among the fields they carry or select. An L2 geometry pulls cells apart without changing the topology. A geometry of order 2 is curved.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Field(space, values, unit=None): unit is the values' physical unit, a string kept in unyt's canonical spelling ("m/s", "m*s**-1" and "m/s^1" are one unit; "1" is "dimensionless"), or None for unknown. The spatial unit is the geometry's, data.unit, and origin is in it. Kernels never see a unit. See Physical Units.

Field(..., unit=), field.unit the values' unit, or None DataSet(..., unit=), data.unit the spatial unit, the geometry field's; uniform_grid, rectilinear_grid and point_cloud take unit=, point_cloud also units={name: unit} OctreeDataSet(..., units={name: unit}), octree.unit, octree.units the fields' units, and the roots' spatial unit convert(data, unit, field=None) a Field in unit (a new field in the same space), or a dataset with its geometry (origin scaled in double precision; images stay images) or a named field in unit, scaled and offset on the device Statistics.unit, .weight_unit, .unit_of(name) the field's and the weights' units, and each statistic's (variances in the square, sum times the weights') interpolate(..., unit=) the function's values' unit, which its code does not say quantities as parameters lengths ("10 cm", (0.1, "m"), a unyt or pint quantity) converted to the spatial unit, isovalues and thresholds to the field's, step sizes to the particles' time unit; a mass, density or velocity given as one quantity brings its unit (see Physical Units) tack.dataset.units canonical, conversion (factor and offset), same, compatible, common, derived (products of powers), delta (degrees Celsius to kelvin for differences), named (Pa*m**3 as J); the registry is unyt's plus ftUS, the US survey foot

Filters that keep a quantity keep its unit (everything carry takes along, project, values_at_centers, traces, magnitude, means, centres in the spatial unit); those that compute one derive it (gradients, products, measures, fluxes, statistics, deposits, SPH, particle times: the table in Physical Units). Positions in two known spatial units do not meet: probe's points, pieces, AMR boxes and octree probes refuse them. The VTK interop maps each array's UNITS_LABEL.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Tack holds no series of steps: a simulation in situ, or a reader's loop, hands filters one step at a time, and each step is a dataset at its time.
